title: Add simplify autorouter preset
description: Adds simplify as a supported autorouter preset, allowing cleanup across all traces without a selector and warns if used without reroutetrue.
body:

- add `simplify` as a supported autorouter preset in both string and config forms

The simplify routing mode operates on existing routes. Selector-free rerouting is intentionally allowed for this preset so users can run cleanup across every trace in the phase.

title: test: reproduce C388883 encoded pin aliases
description: Reproduces a bug where HTML-encoded pin aliases from EasyEDA are incorrectly processed, leading to invalid pin labels in generated components.
body:
## Why

Importing JLCPCB part C388883 (Panasonic EVQP7C01P) exposes a pin-label conversion bug. The EasyEDA payload represents the duplicate switch terminals with HTML-encoded backticks: `1`` and `2``.

The converter currently carries those encoded values directly into the generated component as aliases:

```ts
pin3: ["1`", "1"]
pin4: ["2`", "2"]
```

Those strings do not satisfy the tscircuit pin-label rules. When the generated component is evaluated, core emits `source_property_ignored_warning` entries and excludes both aliases. This means a successful `tsci import` can produce a component containing labels that are rejected when the component is used.

## What this PR adds

- The raw EasyEDA fixture for C388883.
- A focused regression repro that verifies the encoded terminal numbers are present after parsing.
- Assertions showing that the encoded values propagate into the generated TypeScript.
- Assertions for the downstream invalid-pin-label warnings.

This is intentionally a repro-only PR. It does not prescribe whether the eventual converter fix should decode, normalize, or omit these alternate terminal labels; it provides a concrete fixture and failure boundary for evaluating that fix.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C388883-to-ts.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: fix: export all schematic sheets in image downloads
description: Fixes schematic downloads to include all sheets in multi-sheet projects instead of just the firstdefault sheet.
body:
## Motivation

Projects can contain multiple `schematic_sheet` elements, but schematic PNG and SVG downloads used `convertCircuitJsonToSchematicSvg`. That renderer intentionally selects one sheet, so multi-sheet projects downloaded only their first/default sheet—for example, the `host` sheet in `mohan-bee/hub`.

`circuit-to-svg` already provides `convertCircuitJsonToStackedSchematicSheetsSvg`, which renders every sheet in `sheet_index` order and preserves the existing behavior for projects with zero or one sheet.

## Changes

- use `convertCircuitJsonToStackedSchematicSheetsSvg` directly for schematic SVG downloads
- use the same stacked renderer before rasterizing schematic PNG downloads
- use the standard `image/svg+xml` MIME type for SVG downloads

## Result

Schematic PNG and SVG downloads now contain every sheet in one vertically stacked image. Single-sheet projects continue to render normally. PCB, assembly, pinout, and 3D downloads are unchanged.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`
- Biome formatting check on both changed files

## Reference

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/146e12e2-7694-46d5-9fd6-976c578cda0a

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/166b2962-147e-42c7-b056-ee5585cbfda4

description: Summary add numbered AutoroutingPipelineSolver11_Simplification, a cleanup-only pipeline for existing SimpleRouteJson.traces use the conventional BasePipelineSolver definition with explicit prepare, simplify, apply, and DRC-validation stages; the outer pipeline does not override _step() keep stage work incremental: one input trace, one wrapped solver step, one output trace, or one validation pass per _step() preserve variable-width traces exactly and include them as immutable collision geometry while simplifying constant-width traces opt Pipeline 11 into clearance checks that use the actual currentneighbor trace widths and a matching spatial-search margin, without changing established pipeline behavior preserve trace IDs, connection metadata, endpoints, terminal vias, and terminal PCB-port metadata without routing missing SRJ connections  Why The simplify autorouting phase needs a dedicated local pipeline for users who want to improve traces that are already routed. Reusing the normal autorouting pipeline would solve SRJ connections again instead of limiting the work to post-route cleanup. The cleanup solvers currently use one traceThickness per high-density route. Sending a variable-width SRJ trace through that representation collapsed every segment to one arbitrary width and created DRC violations. Pipeline 11 now makes that capability boundary explicit: constant-width routes are simplified, while variable-width routes retain their exact copper geometry and still block unsafe shortcuts. Companion props PR: https:github.comtscircuitpropspull723  Real-board visual snapshot The fixture was captured from the board and MCU autorouting events produced by imrishabh18rp2040-motor-controller(https:tscircuit.comimrishabh18rp2040-motor-controllerfiles) at tscircuitrp2040-motor-controllerb4560e5(https:github.comtscircuitrp2040-motor-controllercommitb4560e5). Pipeline 11 preserves all 148 traces and every input width set, including 30 exact variable-width routes. It reduces route points from 1,829 to 1,763 and vias from 150 to 73, while exact relaxed DRC remains 0  0. !RP2040 motor controller before and after Pipeline 11 simplification(https:raw.githubusercontent.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterfeatsimplification-pipelinetests__snapshots__pipeline11-simplification-rp2040-motor-controller-visual-rp2040-motor-controller-before-after.snap.svg)  Validation bun run build bunx tsc --noEmit focused Pipeline 11 suite: 4 tests passed Pipeline 9 reference-clean exact-output regression test passed real-board test: all width sets preserved, 30 variable-width routes exact, exact relaxed DRC 0  0 visual snapshot regenerated, rendered to PNG, and inspected git diff --check GitHub CI: all 9 test shards, build, type-check, format-check, added-code check, and Vercel checks passed
body:
## Summary

- add numbered `AutoroutingPipelineSolver11_Simplification`, a cleanup-only pipeline for existing `SimpleRouteJson.traces`
- use the conventional `BasePipelineSolver` definition with explicit prepare, simplify, apply, and DRC-validation stages; the outer pipeline does not override `_step()`
- keep stage work incremental: one input trace, one wrapped solver step, one output trace, or one validation pass per `_step()`
- preserve variable-width traces exactly and include them as immutable collision geometry while simplifying constant-width traces
- opt Pipeline 11 into clearance checks that use the actual current/neighbor trace widths and a matching spatial-search margin, without changing established pipeline behavior
- preserve trace IDs, connection metadata, endpoints, terminal vias, and terminal PCB-port metadata without routing missing SRJ connections

## Why

The `simplify` autorouting phase needs a dedicated local pipeline for users who want to improve traces that are already routed. Reusing the normal autorouting pipeline would solve SRJ connections again instead of limiting the work to post-route cleanup.

The cleanup solvers currently use one `traceThickness` per high-density route. Sending a variable-width SRJ trace through that representation collapsed every segment to one arbitrary width and created DRC violations. Pipeline 11 now makes that capability boundary explicit: constant-width routes are simplified, while variable-width routes retain their exact copper geometry and still block unsafe shortcuts.

Companion props PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/723

## Real-board visual snapshot

The fixture was captured from the board and MCU autorouting events produced by [imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller#files) at [`tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller@b4560e5`](https://github.com/tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller/commit/b4560e5).

Pipeline 11 preserves all 148 traces and every input width set, including 30 exact variable-width routes. It reduces route points from **1,829 to 1,763** and vias from **150 to 73**, while exact relaxed DRC remains **0 → 0**.

![RP2040 motor controller before and after Pipeline 11 simplification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/feat/simplification-pipeline/tests/__snapshots__/pipeline11-simplification-rp2040-motor-controller-visual-rp2040-motor-controller-before-after.snap.svg)

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused Pipeline 11 suite: 4 tests passed
- Pipeline 9 reference-clean exact-output regression test passed
- real-board test: all width sets preserved, 30 variable-width routes exact, exact relaxed DRC 0 → 0
- visual snapshot regenerated, rendered to PNG, and inspected
- `git diff --check`
- GitHub CI: all 9 test shards, build, type-check, format-check, added-code check, and Vercel checks passed

title: repro: adjacent passive partitions violate configured gap
description: Reproduces a schematic auto-layout failure where components from adjacent partitions are packed closer than the configured partition gap, causing their rendered annotations to collide.
body: ### Motivation Capture a general schematic auto-layout failure where components from adjacent partitions are packed closer than the configured partition gap, which causes their rendered annotations to collide. The input was captured directly from the exact LedBlinker TSX using @tscircuit/core 0.0.1803 and @tscircuit/matchpack 0.0.88. It preserves the complete generated Matchpack problem and does not add manual schematic positions or a proposed fix. ### Current behavior C1 belongs to a standalone partition while C3 belongs to the main U1 partition. After layout, their body-to-body vertical gap is about 0.105 even though partitionGap is 1.2. In the Core schematic this insufficient separation makes the C1/C3 reference, value, and rail annotations overlap. ### Expected behavior Distinct partitions should retain at least the configured partitionGap after the full layout pipeline, including later alignment passes. ### Scope This is a repro-only draft. It adds the captured InputProblem, a focused assertion that confirms the gap violation, and the current solver snapshot. title: Reroute component-to-component traces around avoidable label-trace crossings
description: Reroutes component-to-component traces to avoid crossings with generated net-label connectors, ensuring cleaner routing and preserving valid label-to-label crossings.
body:
## Root cause

Component-to-component traces are routed before generated net-label connectors are added to the pipeline. A later connector can therefore cross an already-routed component trace even when that component trace has an equally short clean corridor.

Crossings between two generated label connectors are valid and remain unchanged.

## Solution

- track generated connector IDs explicitly instead of matching trace ID strings
- retain provenance for traces produced by the original component-routing pass
- after connectors exist, inspect only crossings between a fixed generated connector and an eligible component trace
- reuse the existing `generatePerpendicularTraceDetours` routing primitive, extended with optional bounds so an attached label and its connector form one obstacle
- accept only candidates that are no longer than the original route, preserve the turn budget, and avoid components, text, foreign labels, coincident traces, and all foreign-trace intersections

The previous standalone 331-line candidate generator has been removed. The cleanup now uses a compact coordinator around the existing routing primitive.

## Result

- the wireless-mouse component trace takes the available collision-free corridor
- generated connectors never move
- label-to-label crossings remain allowed
- routes without an equally short safe alternative remain unchanged
- exactly one visual snapshot changes

## Verification

- focused coverage for a clean component route, an allowed label-to-label crossing, and rejection of a longer detour
- wireless-mouse and TI power-output repro snapshots
- `bun test --timeout 20000` — 297 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed

title: Align same-net pin exits, endpoint buses, and shared rails
description: Aligns adjacent same-side pin exits onto neighboring pin rows, aligns degree-two buses between perpendicular endpointload traces, and preserves generated connector junctions while validating candidates against various criteria.
body:
## Summary

- align adjacent same-side pin exits onto a neighboring pin row when the reroute is shorter and clear
- align degree-two buses between perpendicular endpoint/load traces onto both load rails
- align nearby first rails that leave the same endpoint in the same direction when doing so removes a visible jog
- align eligible generated label-connector rails without moving their labels or host traces
- preserve generated connector junctions when their host trace is aligned
- pass connector provenance from the producing solver instead of parsing trace ID strings
- validate every candidate against components, other-net traces, labels, moved attached labels, endpoint integrity, and newly introduced crossings
- support all rotations and reversed trace/endpoint ordering
- update 28 snapshots where the generic rules produce visually reviewed alignment improvements

## Root causes

The original junction heuristics only accepted reroutes that shortened visible geometry or matched a specialized return-bus topology. They therefore kept nearby parallel rails joined by small jogs even when the topology allowed one continuous rail.

The shared-endpoint candidate is topology-based: both traces must share a pin, depart along the same axis and direction, expose compatible perpendicular rails whose intervals touch after alignment, and keep the branch rail internal so no endpoint moves. Specialized return/bus candidates continue to run first.

Adjacent-pin exit alignment is also topology-based: it derives the departure and stem axes from pin facing directions, finds an outward donor segment shared by the nearby pin rows, and reroutes only when the branch already leaves through that stem. It does not depend on a fixed point count or H/V turn sequence.

Generated net-orientation connectors need two additional cases. An eligible connector can remove its own offset rail when it attaches inside a host segment and the aligned rails meet end-to-end. When a real host trace moves, an attached connector endpoint is projected onto the moved host along its existing segment so the junction remains connected. Connectors attached at donor corners, connectors that would overlap donor rails, and candidates that collide with any component, trace, or label remain unchanged.

## Verification

- `bun test`: 294 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- full non-updating snapshot suite confirms that only the three newly approved SVGs changed in the latest alignment refinement
- focused before/after visual review of the three newly changed snapshots

title: fix: clear copper pours around oval plated holes
description: Fixes the omission of oval plated holes in copper pour calculations, ensuring proper clearance and thermal relief for designs using oval plated holes.
body:
## Why

Circuit JSON supports plated holes with `shape: "oval"`, which are commonly used for through-hole battery contacts and similar elongated terminals. The copper-pour adapter handled circular, pill, and rectangular plated-hole shapes, but it did not convert oval plated holes into solver input pads.

Because the pad was omitted before obstacle processing, the solver had no geometry to subtract from a different-net copper pour. Copper could therefore extend into the required clearance around the plated hole. In the ATTiny85 Arcade Keychain this affected the oval battery pads and prevented the normal exported-board short/clearance validation from being trusted without adding board-specific keepouts.

This behavior should be fixed in the shared solver rather than in individual boards so every design using oval plated holes receives the configured clearance and thermal-relief behavior automatically.

## What changed

- Add an `InputOvalPad` type that preserves the outer width, outer height, position, and rotation from Circuit JSON.
- Convert `pcb_plated_hole` elements with `shape: "oval"` into solver input pads.
- Approximate the rotated ellipse as a polygon and apply the configured pad margin with a rounded geometric offset.
- Include oval plated holes in thermal-relief clearance generation.
- Add a regression test that verifies conversion, rotation, and the resulting 0.2 mm copper-clearance extents.
- Add SVG snapshot coverage for a rotated oval plated hole with four thermal-relief spokes.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 51 passed, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check` — passes with only the existing oversized-fixture warnings

body:
## Summary

- read schematic wire geometry from the public `kicadts` `Wire.points` API and keep KiCad junctions on renderable traces
- place ports with the selected symbol unit/body-style transform and emit matching `source_port` records
- render embedded KiCad symbol primitives, pin names/numbers, and visible reference/value fields instead of generic component boxes
- preserve standalone text, hierarchical sheets and pins, no-connect markers, rectangles, polylines, and arcs
- distinguish plain KiCad local labels from shaped global labels, while retaining their unique `source_net` records
- preserve hierarchical-sheet pin direction markers, readable text orientation, inset placement, and KiCad sheet colors
- update the HSP USB LED and pic-programmer native-KiCad-vs-converted snapshots

## Why

The importer previously read a nonexistent wire property, placed pins relative to the page origin, combined pins from every unit, and discarded most embedded symbol and top-level schematic graphics. Real schematics therefore lost wires, used generic boxes, showed misplaced/duplicated ports, and omitted labels, annotations, grouping graphics, hierarchical sheets, no-connect markers, and visible junctions.

The symbol-local transform now follows KiCad's Cartesian symbol coordinates without applying a second Y inversion. Hidden KiCad property text stays hidden, while visible pin and instance text is preserved. Local labels no longer render as boxed global arrows, and 180-degree sheet pins remain readable instead of appearing upside down.

This PR is stacked on #176 so its diff contains only the conversion fix and its regression coverage.

## Visual regression

Both real-circuit snapshots keep the native KiCad schematic on the left and the converted Circuit JSON schematic on the right. The regressions verify:

- HSP USB LED: 13 wire traces, 1 junction, 23 source/schematic ports, real USB/passive/power symbol geometry, and both source grouping rectangles
- pic-programmer: 131 wire traces, 26 junctions, 182 source/schematic ports, 10 plain local-label instances backed by 7 unique source nets, the hierarchical sheet and its 4 readable pin markers, 6 no-connect markers, and 8 dashed source drawing paths

description: Fixes duplicated traces in the local autorouter stage output by ensuring that the current solver stage returns the correct trace data without reinserting it as new PCB copper.
body:
## Summary

- return the current solver stage from `TscircuitAutorouter`, matching the `GenericLocalAutorouter` contract
- keep cumulative trace data for autorouting phase events without reinserting it as new PCB copper
- honor `__replaces_pcb_trace_id` when accumulating outputs from multiple routing stages

## Why this belongs in core

`capacity-autorouter.getOutputSimpleRouteJson()` intentionally returns a complete Simple Route JSON document, including unchanged preloaded traces. Core's local-autorouter adapter is expected to return the current routing stage, so it should consume `getOutputSimplifiedPcbTraces()` instead. This preserves the upstream API contract and avoids a Pipeline 9-only special case.

## Validation

Against current `main`:

- focused autorouter, fanout, preloaded-phase, cache, and Pipeline 11 tests pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes
- `bun run build` passes
- Biome formatting check passes

- Gameboy reproduction passes
- all trace-count and via-count assertions pass
- multi-phase and preloaded-output adaptation tests pass

This does not address the independent Pipeline 9 reconnection, keepout conflict, differential-pair skew, or Arduino timeout regressions.

title: fix: preserve fanout handoff point identity
description: Fixes the synchronization of PCB breakout point identity on completed fanout traces before the global routing phase, allowing Pipeline 9 to recognize pre-routed copper as connected to the handoff endpoint and removing unnecessary detours in routing.
body:
## Summary

- preserve the synchronized pcb_breakout_point identity on completed fanout traces before the global routing phase
- let Pipeline 9 recognize pre-routed copper as already connected to the handoff endpoint
- remove unnecessary handoff detours in the AM62L-to-LPDDR4 E2E and an existing fanout regression

## Root cause

Core synchronizes each global connection endpoint to the fanout exit, but the completed fanout trace still lists only the phase-local synthetic connection name in connectsTo. The global endpoint uses the persistent pcb_breakout_point id. Pipeline 9 therefore sees coincident geometry without shared connectivity and adds a short reconnecting route.

The synchronization step now maps each phase-local connection name to its persistent breakout point id and adds that id to the completed fanout trace. This changes connectivity metadata at the ownership boundary; it does not add solver overrides, post-process routed geometry, or alter autorouter code.

## Stack

- base E2E: #3602
- this PR is intentionally based on test/am62l-lpddr4-pipeline9-handoff-e2e
- no test or fixture source files change relative to the base PR; the only test-side changes are generated processed PCB SVG snapshots

## Validation

- 184 assertions across the LPDDR4 Pipeline 9 E2E, existing AM62L decoupling board, two breakout-to-global regressions, sequential fanout phases, keepout metadata, and SII9022 HDMI fanout handoff

title: fix: avoid opening lockfiles by default in the editor
description: Fixes the issue where the editor opens lockfiles by default instead of the intended circuit entrypoint files, ensuring that only eligible files are selected for editing.
body:
## Summary

- Use the editor's existing default-file selection rules in the optimized package loader, recognizing `index.ts`, `*.circuit.tsx`, `main.ts(x)`, and other TSX files while excluding lockfiles and generated/hidden files.
- Preserve explicit file selection, including links that intentionally open a lockfile.
- Keep automatic fallbacks safe when a URL references a missing file or contains only lockfiles, and finish loading when there is no eligible default file.

## Root cause

The optimized loader checked only for `index.tsx`, then selected the first file returned by `/package_files/list`. It bypassed `findTargetFile`, which already recognizes circuit entrypoints and excludes lockfiles. Once the priority file was selected, `useFileManagement` retained that selection as the other files arrived.

For [ShiboSoftwareDev/msp430f5503-usb-c-dev-board](https://tscircuit.com/editor?package_id=ceec4b8f-865f-4e81-8937-74c8cfa57d89), the live API returns `bun.lock` first and the circuit entrypoint is `index.circuit.tsx`, so the loader opened `bun.lock`.

Also inspected the related API file-list endpoint and the installed Monaco editor implementation. File order is not an entrypoint contract, and Monaco receives its selected file from this application; no changes to those repositories are needed.

## Verification

- Reproduced the original `bun.lock` selection with a regression test before applying the fix.
- `bun test`: 314 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed (includes 25 selection regression tests).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Biome formatting checks on all changed files: passed.
- `bunx playwright test playwright-tests/editor-default-file.spec.ts --workers=1 --retries=0 --reporter=line`: 4 passed.
  - Circuit entrypoint selected even when the lockfile loads first.
  - Explicit `file_path=bun.lock` remains supported.
  - Lockfile-only packages finish loading without a default selection.
  - Lockfile-only URL hashes do not reopen the first file.

title: fix: serialize concurrent tsci add installations
description: Serializes concurrent tsci add invocations to prevent overlapping package-manager processes that can race on package.json, lockfiles, and native dependency installation.
body:
Concurrent `tsci add` invocations in the same project currently start overlapping package-manager processes. This can race on `package.json`, lockfiles, `node_modules`, and native dependency installation. This was encountered when an agent issued three add calls in parallel during circuit generation.

Serialize adds with a project-scoped `proper-lockfile` lock, covering registry configuration, installation, and KiCad setup. Resolve the project real path so symlinked working directories share the lock. Release it on failure and recover stale locks after interrupted processes. Run install subprocesses asynchronously so long installs continue refreshing the lock heartbeat; serialize KiCad setup within multi-package adds as well.

Validation:

- New subprocess regression fails on the base branch with overlapping installs (`EEXIST`) and passes with this change. Covers a 12-second install exceeding the stale threshold, symlinked working directories, failure release, and stale-lock recovery.

title: fix: report autorouting pipeline progress
description: Fixes the autorouting progress reporting for Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9, ensuring accurate progress updates during routing operations.
body:
Autorouter diagnostics report `progress=0%` even as routing advances through pathing and high-density routing. In [this adm6-breakout release](https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/adm6-breakout/releases/65f0a6dd-aa34-490b-8f26-526a3db9442c), the captured logs contain 59 zero-percent routing updates; the separate fanout solver reports 100%.

Core's `TscircuitAutorouter` forwards the top-level solver's `progress`. Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9 inherit `BaseSolver.progress = 0` but do not implement `computeProgress()`, so that value never changes. Pipeline 9 Networked inherits the same issue from Pipeline 9.

Implement `computeProgress()` directly on Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9. It combines completed pipeline steps with the active solver's progress. Pipeline 9 Networked receives the calculation through inheritance. Routing behavior is unchanged.

Steps have equal weight: this is a completion indicator, not a time estimate. A step without its own progress estimate advances the percentage when it finishes.

Validation:
- A focused test verifies nonzero progress for Pipeline 7, Pipeline 9, and Pipeline 9 Networked.
- Existing Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9 Networked contract tests pass.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` pass.

After release, consumers must refresh `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` in the core/runtime bundle. Core's progress-event implementation does not need a code change; this PR does not update the deployed builder.

title: fix: accept same-net copper at Pipeline 9 handoffs
description: Fixes autorouters relaxed DRC to accept trace endpoints only when they geometrically touch same-net copper on the same PCB layer, preventing false disconnected endpoint errors.
body:
## Summary

- make autorouter's relaxed DRC accept a trace endpoint only when it geometrically touches same-net copper on the same PCB layer
- keep every real disconnected endpoint and every non-continuity DRC error unchanged
- add focused coverage for a global net-level trace joining two preloaded fanout traces

## Why

Pipeline 9 receives valid phase-boundary routes whose endpoints touch preloaded fanout copper and share the same logical source trace. The pinned checks implementation only recognizes pad-connected net-level endpoints, so joint DRC repair sees four false disconnected endpoints and mutates clean parallel DDR routes into a real overlap.

The adapter now verifies the trace net through the existing connectivity map, indexes non-degenerate wire segments by net and layer, and removes only an exact `disconnected_endpoint_<trace>_<side>` result whose endpoint is within the two traces' combined copper radii. This is geometry-backed connectivity, not an error-message allowlist or repair fallback.

I evaluated upgrading `@tscircuit/checks` first. The first release with equivalent endpoint semantics also enables stricter terminal-layer validation and exposes two unrelated existing router defects (`bugreport88` and Pipeline 7 sample169), so this PR keeps the repository's established dependency instead of hiding those real errors or expanding scope.

Full two-component processed-SVG E2E: tscircuit/core#3609

title: Reuse static connectivity during Pipeline9 DRC repair
description: Reuses static connectivity during DRC repair in Pipeline9 to improve performance and reduce timeouts.
body:
Pipeline9 repeatedly rebuilt connection metadata and scanned multilayer obstacle connectivity for every DRC repair candidate. Pipeline7 already retains that prepared converter. Reuse it throughout Pipeline9's joint repair stage, while converting each candidate's geometry afresh.

The reported SRJ18 runs completed 13/16 boards with Pipeline7 versus 11/16 with Pipeline9. Both additional Pipeline9 timeouts, samples 2 and 12, were in joint DRC repair after high-density routing had finished. [Original Pipeline7 run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33661933114) · [Original Pipeline9 run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33661945494).

## Same-machine SRJ18 results

[Benchmark run and raw reports](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33668815739): main `0f0fd848` and PR `e1542c99`, run sequentially on one 8-vCPU Blacksmith machine, 16 samples, effort 1, concurrency 4, 360s per-sample timeout. The subsequent commit only wraps a test assertion; production code is identical.

| Metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed | 12/16 (75.0%) | **13/16 (81.3%)** |
| Timeouts | 2 | **1** |
| P50 | 94.9s | **85.8s (-9.6%)** |
| P95 | 360.0s | **339.4s (-5.7%)** |
| Relaxed DRC passes | 8/16 | 8/16 |
| DRC issues, 12 boards completed by both | 74 | 74 |
| Vias, 12 boards completed by both | 2,250 | 2,250 |

Sample 2 now completes in **328.2s**. Sample 12 already finishes on main in this controlled run, but falls from **343.2s to 253.3s**; its joint repair stage falls from **113.7s to 54.8s (-51.8%)**. Sample 8's repair stage falls from 95.5s to 53.0s. Total time on the 12 boards completed by both falls from 1,367.3s to 1,190.2s (-13.0%). There are no outcome regressions, and every common completed board retains its individual DRC and via counts.

The aggregate DRC total rises from 74 to 86 and average vias from 187.50 to 211.23 because the newly completed sample 2 contributes 12 DRC issues and 496 vias. It remains DRC-failing; relaxed DRC passes stay at 8/16. The remaining sample 6 timeout occurs in high-density routing, and samples 14/15 fail upstream pathing in both revisions.

## Validation

title: Fix Bug Report 94 trace overlap in force solver
description: Fixes trace overlap issue in the force solver related to Bug Report 94, ensuring no overlaps remain in the autorouting process.
body: ## Before ## After ## Summary - pin `high-density-repair01` to the fix in https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair01/pull/17 - run the Bug Report 94 regression explicitly through `AutoroutingPipelineSolver9_PreloadedTraceGraph` - require at most 5 DRC errors and assert that neither the original `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` overlap nor a transferred overlap involving `source_trace_108` remains - update the deterministic macOS and Linux Pipeline9 snapshots ## Where the issue was The overlap is visible at the `highDensityRepairSolver` phase because that phase consumes the immediately preceding `highDensityForceImproveSolver` output. The bad geometry was already present in that input; the repair stage did not create it. Inside the actual `HighDensityForceImproveSolver`, the first force pass created the `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` proper crossing. The existing guarded rerun removed that pair but moved the collision to `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_99`, leaving the total DRC count at 6. This is why a visually clear snapshot and a passing `<= 6` assertion did not prove the defect was fixed. The upstream solver now validates residual route-pair clearance, restores a small aligned corridor from the original topology, adjusts only a newly affected neighbor when required, and accepts the candidate only when protected pairs remain clear and the local violation count strictly decreases. ## Why a later phase is not the primary fix A focused run of the existing `highDensityRepairSolver` on only the offending node left the `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` centerline distance effectively at zero, so merely increasing repair samples does not address this interior crossing. Pipeline9's later joint/reference DRC repair remains useful as a safety net, but it runs after stitching and simplification and is not guaranteed to select this local collision region. Fixing the geometry in the actual force solver removes the defect before every downstream phase and benefits every pipeline that uses that solver. ## Validation - focused Bug Report 94 Pipeline9 test on macOS: 5 DRC errors, no overlap involving `source_trace_108`, 2,578,699 iterations, 84.6 s - Linux CI Bug Report 94 Pipeline9 shard: same DRC/no-overlap assertions passed and the Pipeline9 snapshot was accepted - autorouter CI: build, type-check, format, Vercel, and all 9 Bun test shards passed - upstream solver CI: format, test, and type-check passed ## Pipeline9 same-machine benchmark Command: `/benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine` - [`dataset01` (85 scenarios)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33567287294): 100% completion, 100% relaxed DRC pass, 0 DRC issues, 0 timeouts, and 0 outcome regressions on both main and PR - [`srj18` (16 scenarios)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33567288855): completion, relaxed DRC pass, and timeouts unchanged; 0 improved and 0 regressed outcomes; aggregate DRC issues changed from 74 to 75, isolated to `sample004`

## Problem

The `seveibar/smd-usb-c` connector is visible in tscircuit, but its body is missing from the exported KiCad board. The component supplies an OBJ model only; `create3DModelsFromCadComponent` selects STEP or WRL and returns no model for this input.

## Reproduction and motivation

Adds a single-connector, top-side board using a vendored copy of the actual component. Circuit JSON is generated through `Circuit`, and model packaging is explicitly enabled. This isolates the format limitation from bottom-side rotation, model download failures, and viewer settings.

The repro confirms one footprint and 22 pad/hole entries survive export, while model references and model downloads are both empty. It includes a PCB input snapshot, an actual KiCad 3D render, and a structural snapshot of the model data. The accompanying note documents fixture provenance and how to reproduce the result.

This PR records the current omission; it does not implement a fix. The characterization test passes when the omission is reproduced. Its assertions should change when a supported model, conversion, or explicit unsupported-format handling is introduced. The motivation is to make missing mechanical models visible and reproducible before choosing that remedy.

Input PCB footprint:

The right panel is the final HighDensityForceImproveSolver result: the original crossing is removed without transferring the overlap to source_trace_99. This image is the committed test artifact from tests__snapshots__bugreport94-force-crossing.snap.svg; the test also asserts the corresponding centerline clearances numerically.  Summary fix Bug Report 94 in the actual HighDensityForceImproveSolver detect proper segment-interior crossings left by the guarded force rerun recover a small route corridor from the original topology, aligned to the force result project only newly affected neighboring routes and accept a candidate only when protected pairs stay clear and the local violation count decreases add a focused regression for source_trace_108 against both source_trace_138 and source_trace_99  Root cause The force solver enforced point-to-segment clearance without preserving segment-pair topology. Adjacent points could remain individually valid while two segment interiors swapped sides and crossed. The existing guarded rerun removed the original source_trace_108  source_trace_138 crossing, but its whole-node movement transferred the overlap to source_trace_108  source_trace_99. The output therefore looked improved in the snapshot while the final DRC count remained 6. This change adds a post-rerun acceptance step. It reconstructs only the crossing corridor from the original non-crossing topology, aligns it to the fixed force-result segment, resolves any newly touched neighbor locally, and rejects candidates that restore a protected overlap or fail to reduce the number of violating route pairs.  Validation bun test  15 passed, 0 failed bun run typecheck  passed upstream format, test, and typecheck CI  passed full autorouter Bug Report 94  5 DRC errors, no trace-overlap error involving source_trace_108
body:
## Visual reproduction

![Bug Report 94 before and after force improvement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair01/f29ff705b019dc8a18bd2560aa6fe61124b1f543/tests/__snapshots__/bugreport94-force-crossing.snap.svg)

Red is `source_trace_108`, blue is `source_trace_138`, and green is neighboring `source_trace_99`. The left panel is the raw force-pass result, where `source_trace_108` crosses `source_trace_138`. The right panel is the final `HighDensityForceImproveSolver` result: the original crossing is removed without transferring the overlap to `source_trace_99`.

This image is the committed test artifact from `tests/__snapshots__/bugreport94-force-crossing.snap.svg`; the test also asserts the corresponding centerline clearances numerically.

## Summary

- fix Bug Report 94 in the actual `HighDensityForceImproveSolver`
- detect proper segment-interior crossings left by the guarded force rerun
- recover a small route corridor from the original topology, aligned to the force result
- project only newly affected neighboring routes and accept a candidate only when protected pairs stay clear and the local violation count decreases
- add a focused regression for `source_trace_108` against both `source_trace_138` and `source_trace_99`

## Root cause

The force solver enforced point-to-segment clearance without preserving segment-pair topology. Adjacent points could remain individually valid while two segment interiors swapped sides and crossed.

The existing guarded rerun removed the original `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` crossing, but its whole-node movement transferred the overlap to `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_99`. The output therefore looked improved in the snapshot while the final DRC count remained 6.

This change adds a post-rerun acceptance step. It reconstructs only the crossing corridor from the original non-crossing topology, aligns it to the fixed force-result segment, resolves any newly touched neighbor locally, and rejects candidates that restore a protected overlap or fail to reduce the number of violating route pairs.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 15 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck` — passed
- upstream format, test, and typecheck CI — passed

body:
AM62L progressive routing can stall after the fanout-solver update: the initial dense route strands a signal, then repeatedly searches winding paths in a synchronous fallback that prevents Bun's test timeout from firing. Core CI hits its 15-minute job limit.

Retry coordinated routing before the broad fallback, cache A* edge-clearance checks per terminal, and retain ordinary dogbone candidates when automatically matched sites fail. This restores the complete progressive route and one via per connection in the two-bus DRAM case.

Route both top-facing layouts with their original timing constraints:
- Repro 04: route all 135 connections and plane drops before length tuning. Its test no longer removes differential pairs or skew limits.
- Dataset-fanout31 sample 02-top-center: add the exact capture and a debugger sample with explicit plane reservation hints. Route all 135 connections with 135 through-vias, keeping all original geometry, differential pairs, bus skew limits, and 102 plane terminations.

The centered case also requires consistent clearance handling when a winding path leaves its own source pad, corner-aware boundary vias, and joint selection of plane routes when a greedy choice blocks another drop. Enumerate singleton plane candidates once instead of repeatedly regenerating their prefixes. For length matching, revisit excessive detours against completed copper and allow a differential pair's outer lane to move aside before tuning its mate. Searches retain bounded attempts, and complete copper is revalidated before accepting a result.

Validation:
- Top-center regression: 135 connections, 135 through-vias, full routed-copper DRC and original timing constraints pass; 34.7 seconds locally on Bun 1.4.0 and 101.0 seconds in CI. Includes SVG snapshot and capture generator.
- Constrained Repro 04 passes with its existing snapshot in 7.5 seconds locally and 24.4 seconds in CI, previously 36.2 seconds locally.
- RAM-left full solve retains its snapshot. Progressive capture passes full DRC with its existing snapshot. Configured corner routing is isolated so the ordinary progressive fanout remains identical to the previously passing output. Typecheck and formatting pass.
- Single-pass enumeration reproduces all 136 previously captured plane candidates exactly and in order.
- Earlier Bun CPU profiles of the initial timeout fix reduced the isolated solve from 11.6 to 5.3 seconds with collision caching alone; the published 0.0.51 case was still searching at 30 seconds. Those measurements precede the additional top-facing fixes.
- Final solver commit 9da1d4c passes all eight test shards, typecheck, formatting, and Vercel. Core commit 40ba64e also passes all ten test shards, typecheck, formatting, smoke test, and Vercel with the final pin.

Core dependency update: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3605

Route all **135/135 AM62L fanout connections** in the RAM-left `11-left-center` sample from [dataset-fanout31-am62l](https://github.com/tscircuit/dataset-fanout31-am62l/blob/8c73befb36b125c84651c07454a9b940b3c6500a/samples/11-left-center.tsx), with no validation issues. The complete case takes about 46 seconds locally on the first layer assignment.

The captured input is unchanged: all 573 pad obstacles, 102 plane drops, nine DDR signal buses, three differential pairs, and original clearance and length-skew constraints are retained. The upstream sample contains no decoupling capacitors.

**Scope:** AM62L fanout only; this does not complete the RAM fanout or inter-chip DDR routing.

## Routing changes

- Align the fine winding grid to the pad lattice to find narrow inter-via channels, and add bounded blocked-terminal route-order retries.
- Coordinate dogbone sites and avoid reserving corner-bus vias inside a neighboring wide bus's source field.
- Let an embedded singleton such as RESET escape on its source layer, then use one via near the boundary to reach its assigned layer.
- Match plane sites against the actual routed copper, retaining provisional sites when possible during length matching.
- Preserve the existing explicitly configured dense-routing path and small-bus ordering.

## Reproduction and visual coverage

- Add Dataset 08 with the exact upstream input, a pinned TSX/core capture script, and a timeout-bounded diagnostic CLI.
- Add input, BYTE1, planes-plus-address, and full-solve SVG regression tests using `solver.visualize()`.
- Refresh two existing SoC routing snapshots for the new valid route geometry; the prior top-edge repro keeps its existing snapshot.

```sh
bun scripts/solve-fanout31-left.ts --timeout-ms 120000 --max-layer-combinations 1 --output /tmp/fanout31-left
```

title: Add all-sample benchmarks and /benchmark PR workflow
description: Add a new benchmarking workflow that runs all available samples, records results, and provides a status update via PR comments.
body:
## Summary

- Extend `./benchmark.sh` and `bun run benchmark` to run every available sample: Datasets 01–08, SRJ19, and SRJ29 (**421 samples** today).
- Run samples in isolated processes with bounded parallelism and a hard per-sample timeout. Crashes, unsolved cases, and timeouts are recorded without preventing later samples from running.
- Save ordered, incremental JSON and Markdown reports with the commit, search configuration, dataset totals, per-sample status, timing, and validation counts.
- Add a `/benchmark` PR-comment workflow on a **32-vCPU Blacksmith ARM** runner that updates a status comment with results and links to the full report artifacts.

## Usage

```sh
./benchmark.sh
./benchmark.sh --list
./benchmark.sh --dataset dataset08
./benchmark.sh --concurrency 8 --sample-timeout-seconds 300
```

Local defaults are up to four processes and a 120-second per-sample deadline. Circuit constraints and sample-specific assignment budgets are preserved unless the search budget is explicitly overridden. SRJ29 retains its original-endpoint connectivity and independent emitted-copper DRC checks; fanout-only successes are not presented as completed inter-chip routing.

The dedicated `bun run benchmark:srj29` command and existing SRJ29 workflow remain available.

## PR automation

An exact `/benchmark` comment from a non-bot user with current repository write, maintain, or admin access captures the PR head SHA and queues the benchmark. Manual dispatch is also supported.

PR code executes in a read-only job without persisted checkout credentials. A separate job checks out the trusted workflow revision, validates the report as data, and posts results. No custom bot secret is required. Complete and partial reports are uploaded, and infrastructure failures are reported to the PR.

**Activation:** the comment trigger becomes available after this workflow is merged into the default branch. The Blacksmith/comment round trip has not been run yet.

## Validation

- Seven new tests pass, covering catalog completeness, CLI reports, process timeouts/crashes, SRJ29 validation, comment authorization, report rendering, and workflow permission separation.
- Typecheck, format check, `bash -n`, and actionlint pass (Blacksmith's custom runner label is explicitly allowed during actionlint verification).
- A two-second-per-sample infrastructure smoke sweep visited **all 421 samples** and produced complete reports: 83 solved, 338 timed out, no worker errors. This deliberately short run is not a solve-rate baseline.
- AM62L through the new runner with the normal timeout: **135/135 connections solved in 47.85 seconds**.
- Dedicated legacy SRJ29 sample001 still passes all endpoint and copper DRC checks.

title: fix: derive CAD component size from model bounds
description: Fixes incorrect CAD component size calculation by deriving dimensions from the models bounding box instead of PCB footprint dimensions, ensuring accurate rendering of components.
body:
## Summary

- derive `cad_component.size` from the CAD model's own bounding-box extents when model bounds are available
- validate that every derived dimension is finite and positive, while preserving the existing fallback for models without usable bounds
- update the C165948 regression assertion and 3D snapshot to show the connector at its correct scale

## Why this change is needed

This is the fix for the behavior reproduced in #539.

The Parts Engine uses `convertEasyEdaJsonToCircuitJson` directly, so the emitted `cad_component.size` is preserved. Before this change, that size was assembled from the PCB footprint width and height plus an EasyEDA SVG height value. Those measurements describe different coordinate spaces and do not represent the OBJ model's local bounds.

For C165948, the OBJ metadata reports local bounds of approximately **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, while the converter emitted **8.750224 × 5.648262 × 7.899984 mm**. Because the renderer uses `model_object_fit: "contain_within_bounds"`, the undersized 5.648262 mm Y constraint forced a uniform scale of roughly 0.715. The USB-C body was therefore rendered too small, leaving its shell mounting pads outside the model.

The generated-TSX path did not expose the bug because its `cadModel` output omits `size`; the direct Circuit JSON path used by the Parts Engine did.

## Implementation

When explicit `cadModelBounds` or embedded `_objMetadata.bounds` are available, the converter now calculates each local model dimension as `max - min` and uses those values for `cad_component.size`. It only accepts dimensions that are finite and greater than zero. If valid model bounds are unavailable, the converter retains the previous footprint-based fallback to avoid changing behavior for metadata-free models.

For C165948, the emitted size is now **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, preventing unintended scaling and aligning the rendered connector body with its footprint.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-soup-tests/c165948-cad-footprint-size-repro.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-soup-tests` — 28 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

The repository-wide test run was also attempted; unrelated existing snapshot mismatches/timeouts were encountered in other component fixtures, and a later network-dependent conversion stalled. The focused converter suite covering this code path passes completely.

title: test: reproduce C165948 CAD footprint size mismatch
description: Adds a regression test for the C165948 CAD footprint size mismatch issue, recording the incorrect emitted CAD size metadata and providing a 3D snapshot for visibility.
body:
## Summary

- add a regression test for the direct EasyEDA-to-Circuit-JSON conversion of C165948
- record the incorrect emitted CAD size metadata
- add a 3D snapshot with a PCB beneath the part so the CAD-to-footprint mismatch is immediately visible

## Why this PR is needed

Using `<connector standard="usb_c" />` resolves C165948 through the Parts Engine. That flow calls `convertEasyEdaJsonToCircuitJson` directly and preserves the generated `cad_component.size`.

For C165948, the OBJ metadata describes bounds of approximately **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, but the converter emits a CAD target size of **8.750224 × 5.648262 × 7.899984 mm**. The target X/Y values come from the PCB component bounds and do not describe the OBJ in its local coordinate frame. With `model_object_fit: "contain_within_bounds"`, the 3D renderer uses the limiting Y ratio (`5.648262 / 7.90 ≈ 0.715`) and uniformly shrinks the entire USB-C model. The footprint remains at its correct size, leaving the shell mounting pads visibly outside the rendered body.

There is already a C165948 3D test in the repository, but it converts through generated TSX. That generated `cadModel` does not include the problematic `size`, so it cannot reproduce the Parts Engine behavior. This new test deliberately exercises the direct Circuit JSON path used in production.

This PR only adds the reproduction and expected failing-state snapshot. It does not change converter behavior; a follow-up fix can update the asserted dimensions and snapshot.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-soup-tests/c165948-cad-footprint-size-repro.test.ts`

title: Add autorouted physical-via export regression coverage
description: Adds regression tests and fixtures for physical-via export without altering existing implementations or introducing new production code.
body:
## Regression-only PR — the fixes are already merged

The actual fixes landed in [#158](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/158) (physical layer precedence) and [#159](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/159) (drill deduplication). Both are already merged into `main`.

This PR now targets current `main` and adds **only** the automatically generated fixture, provenance, three regression tests and two snapshots. Its production source and package metadata are identical to `main`. It does not replace or reapply the merged implementations.

**Merge guidance:** only this regression PR remains to consider for Gerber, because both fixes have already landed. There is no pending Gerber fix to stack above it. Normally the order is repro first, fix second; the upstream merges happened before this restructuring.

No coordinates, trace paths, copper pours, widths, or board dependencies are patched. The existing PR URL was retained.

## Reproduction

The committed fixture is unmodified output from published `tscircuit@0.0.2462`: two resistor-to-inner1 GND connections generated by automatic fanout on a four-layer board. Both physical vias span top–bottom, but their routing transitions stop at inner1. No PCB paths, manual traces, or manually placed routing vias were used.

This small fixture reproduces the export defect seen on the **complete RP2350 development board**, not merely its MCU essentials subcircuit. It is not itself a complete replica of that board.

![Generated fixture, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/physical-via-drill-spans/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/physical-via-spans-top.snap.svg)
![Generated fixture, bottom through-via annuli](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/physical-via-drill-spans/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/physical-via-spans-bottom.snap.svg)

## Verification

Same machine, same inputs, old unfixed baseline `8af19f5c2e51459c4293c808fc1859beb92c653c` versus current upstream implementation `fa0a968` plus this regression coverage. Rechecked at this PR's `187bb0b` head:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three automatic-via regressions | 0 pass / 3 fail | 3 pass / 0 fail |
| Full test suite, including new regressions | 80 pass / 3 fail on old baseline | 113 pass / 0 fail on current main plus these tests |
| Package build + declarations | — | Pass |
| Typecheck | — | Pass |
| Two-via generated fixture | Incorrect `Plated,1,2,PTH` | Correct `Plated,1,4,PTH` |
| Complete RP2350 trial 19 | Four plated drill spans; 197 plated operations | One top–bottom plated span; 196 plated operations |
| Trial 19 non-plated locating holes | 2 × 0.65 mm | Unchanged |

Regression coverage includes reversed layer ordering, physical blind/buried spans, missing legacy layer lists, duplicated standalone vias, route-defined drill dimensions, and route-only inputs.

The current improvements are provided by merged #158/#159, **not new production code in this PR**. Build and typecheck were rerun and pass. Fresh CI runs apply to `187bb0b`; the earlier full-green run was on the superseded `7f3cd51` head.

Native KiCad drill export independently agrees on trial 19's physical inventory: **148 via holes + 44 header holes + 4 USB shell slots**, all through-board, plus two NPTH locating holes.

These are export checks, **not a claim that the RP2350 is fabrication-ready**. That local working trial still has five native routing/clearance errors and one shorted-net group. The board remains on unmodified published dependencies; no manufacturing order or project upload was made.

title: fix: deduplicate via drill hits and reconcile trace fallbacks
description: Fixes duplicate drill operations in Gerber file exports by deduplicating via drill records based on exact coordinates and drill diameter, ensuring accurate representation of physical vias without unnecessary fallback drills.
body:
## Summary

- Deduplicate via drill records by exact X/Y coordinates, drill diameter, and normalized physical layer span.
- Index explicit vias by position and diameter, then omit trace-derived fallback drills when one existing physical barrel covers the route transition. This works regardless of record ordering or trace IDs, since multiple traces may share a via.
- Preserve different drill sizes, distinct explicit or route-only spans, stacked barrels, nearby coordinates, and unmatched route-only vias. Non-via holes and slots are unchanged.
- Add 16 focused regression cases asserting structured Excellon commands plus a direct output-assertion test for the public Gerber/Excellon file exporter. No custom parsers, SVG generation, or snapshot assertions are used in these tests.

## Before / after snapshots

These snapshots use the **same five-location synthetic fixture and renderer**, counting operations parsed from the actual Excellon files. A normal PCB image hides coincident duplicate drills; this diagnostic makes the emitted hit counts and their layer spans visible.

### Before — 9 operations for 5 physical via locations

Captured from unmodified main at `1d49436` (`v0.0.102`) before applying the fix. Repeated records, explicit-via/route overlap, and a spurious shorter drill produce four redundant operations.

![Before: nine drill operations, including duplicate hits and a spurious blind drill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/0479b7fd0b5d99b0723fc890ce54dac887979c35/tests/excellon-drill/assets/via-drill-deduplication-before.svg)

### After — 5 operations, one per physical via

The genuine L1–L2 blind via and L2–L3 buried route-only via remain. Only duplicate hits and the unnecessary shorter fallback drill disappear.

![After: five drill operations with genuine blind and buried vias preserved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/0479b7fd0b5d99b0723fc890ce54dac887979c35/tests/excellon-drill/__snapshots__/via-drill-deduplication.snap.svg)

These images are retained solely as PR illustrations, linked to the earlier commit that captured them. Snapshot assets and rendering code have been removed from the current diff. The tests now assert exported drill commands, diameters, physical spans, and the exact drill-operation sequences directly.

## Verification

- Regression cases reproduce duplicate hits and incorrect fallback drill spans on the unpatched exporter.
- `bun test`: **110 pass, 0 fail**, including 17 new cases.
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- `bun run build`: pass, including declarations.
- `bun run format:check`: exits successfully; existing oversized JSON fixture notice only.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

This is an export-only fix: no routing, coordinates, copper geometry, or dependency versions are changed.

title: fix: prefer physical layers over legacy via drill endpoints
description: Fixes incorrect drill file generation by prioritizing physical layer spans over deprecated routing endpoints during Gerber file export.
body: ## Summary - Determine plated drill spans from the physical `layers` list before consulting deprecated `from_layer` / `to_layer` fields. - Retain normalized legacy endpoints when physical layers are missing or empty, and the through-board default when no span metadata is present. - Add 12 focused regressions for Gerber-file export, 2/4/6/8-layer through-vias, unsorted physical layers, actual blind/buried spans, legacy compatibility, single-span filtering, and input immutability. - Add a visual regression that compares exported bottom copper with the actual through-board Excellon drill openings. ## Problem During Bluetooth pedometer fabrication export, a physical through-via could have `layers: ["top", "inner1", "inner2", "bottom"]` while its deprecated routing endpoints described only a top-to-inner1 transition. The exporter preferred those endpoints and incorrectly emitted `drill-L1-L2.drl` rather than `drill-L1-L4.drl` with `Plated,1,4,PTH` metadata. Physical layer bounds now determine the drilled barrel. This change is limited to span precedence; drill-hit deduplication and trace-route fallback behavior are unchanged. ## Before / after snapshots The same three-via fixture is rendered from actual exported bottom copper (gold) and through-board drill openings (dark). All three vias physically span L1–L4. The left and center vias have conflicting legacy routing endpoints; the rightmost via is an unchanged control. | Before: unpatched exporter | After: physical-layer precedence | | --- | --- | | | | | Incorrect L1–L2 and L2–L3 drills leave two bottom pads without through holes. | All three holes are in the single L1–L4 drill file. | The **before** image was generated with the exporter source restored to baseline `8af19f5`, not simulated. The **after** image is the checked-in expectation in the [snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/5a86fbd145db7776d61ecb560376f393f810b03c/tests/gerber/generate-gerber-with-physical-via-layer-precedence.test.ts). [Capture details](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/5a86fbd145db7776d61ecb560376f393f810b03c/tests/gerber/assets/physical-via-layer-precedence-snapshots.md). ## Verification - Original 12 regression cases against unmodified main (`8af19f5`): **3 pass, 9 fail**. - New visual regression fails on the unpatched exporter and detects the before/after image difference; the corrected snapshot passes without update mode. - `bun test` with the fix: **93 pass, 0 fail**, including all 13 new cases. - `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`: pass. - `bun run build`: pass, including declarations. - `bun run format:check`: exits successfully; existing oversized JSON fixture notice only. - `git diff --check`: pass.

title: Reproduce flipped bottom-mounted display model in KiCad
description: Adds a characterization reproduction for a bottom-mounted display model in KiCad, isolating the model transform issue without fixing it.
body: ## Problem and motivation A bottom-mounted HS154L03W2C01 display shows its rear PCB and ribbon connector in KiCad instead of its screen. This repro isolates the side-dependent model transform so it can be corrected without changing the intended footprint placement. ## Reproduction Adds two independent boards with the same display, STEP asset, position, and `pcbRotation={180}`. Only the mounting layer changes. The top control is rendered from above; the bottom case is rendered from below. | Case | Input CAD rotation | Exported local model rotation | Actual visible face | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Top | `(0, 0, 180)` | `(0, 0, 0)` | Screen | | Bottom | `(0, 180, 180)` | `(0, 180, 0)` | Rear PCB | Both exports contain the model and all eight pad/hole entries. The exporter retains the bottom-side CAD Y rotation inside a footprint already assigned to `B.Cu`, consistent with applying the side flip twice. Expected behavior is an outward-facing screen on either mounting side. The complete fix should validate both rotation and offset conversion. This PR adds a characterization repro, not a fix. A passing test records the current wrong bottom orientation. It generates Circuit JSON through `Circuit` and changes only the model path for local loading, preserving exported transforms. The original STEP model is included as a losslessly compressed, checksum-verified fixture (about 2 MB) for offline runs. Fixture sources and reproduction steps are listed below. ## Snapshots ## Validation - Repro, existing model export test, and bottom-footprint-layer test: 3 passed, 29 assertions. - Repro rerun against saved snapshots: passed. - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed. - Both rendered model faces visually inspected. - KiCad CLI 10.0.5; Bun 1.3.14. Run: `bun test tests/pcb/repros/repro32-display-bottom-model-rotation.test.tsx`

title: Export EasyEDA OBJ-only models through STEP siblings
description: Fixes the omission of 3D models in KiCad exports for components that only have OBJ URLs by deriving and embedding corresponding STEP models from EasyEDA.
body:
Follow-up fix for the merged repro in #496.

## Problem

The `seveibar/smd-usb-c` connector supplies only an OBJ URL from tscircuit's EasyEDA model CDN. KiCad export previously retained its footprint and pads but silently omitted its 3D body.

## Fix

For OBJ URLs on `modelcdn.tscircuit.com`, derive the corresponding EasyEDA `.step` sibling and pass it through the existing model download and packaging flow. This supports current `/assets/<part>.obj` URLs and the legacy `/download?...&pn=<part>` form.

The fallback is restricted to the recognized tscircuit CDN. Arbitrary OBJ URLs remain unsupported, and explicit STEP or WRL URLs retain priority.

## Regression coverage

The repro uses a vendored copy of the actual USB-C component and verifies that the source has OBJ only. It now requires:

- one exported footprint and all 22 pad/hole entries;
- one packaged `C165948.step` model;
- the correct `${KIPRJMOD}` model reference and download URL;
- successful rendering of the actual model in KiCad.

The exact STEP asset is included as a compressed, checksum-verified offline fixture.

![KiCad render with USB-C model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-to-kicad/142ab58bae6913d1f748b8202d7faaaa41db84a0/tests/pcb/repros/__snapshots__/repro31-usb-c-kicad-3d-missing-model.snap.png)

## Validation

- Repro plus existing model and remote STEP tests: 3 passed, 25 assertions.
- URL-boundary regression: passed (8 cases covering modern/legacy CDN URLs, malformed/unrelated URLs, and explicit STEP precedence).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- KiCad CLI 10.0.5 loaded and rendered the STEP model.

- preserve existing Node and Bun process environment behavior
- add regression coverage for runtimes where process is unavailable

## Why

tscircuit.com runs the solver in a browser Web Worker. Dense fanout routing reads optional debug flags from process.env, but browsers do not define the Node process global, causing routing to abort with process is not defined.

- browser-target bundle imports successfully with globalThis.process removed

title: fix(schematic): normalize wrapped arc sweeps
description: Fixes rendering of Altium schematic arcs to correctly handle angles crossing zero degrees, ensuring accurate representation of wrapped arcs.
body:
Motive: Render Altium schematic arcs correctly when their angles cross zero degrees.

Altium arcs use a positive counterclockwise sweep, but the SVG renderer treated angles such as 360° to 90° as a −270° sweep instead of 90°, causing magnetic-core inductors and other wrapped arcs to appear distorted. This PR normalizes the arc sweep using a reusable helper, preserves full circles, and updates the relevant tests and snapshots without component-specific hardcoding or hacks.

title: fix: update copper-pour-solver for oval plated-hole clearance
description: Fixes copper pour solver to respect clearance around oval plated holes, preventing different-net pours from extending into required pad clearances.
body:
## Why

Copper pours need to respect the clearance around oval plated holes, such as elongated through-hole battery contacts. The previous solver omitted `pcb_plated_hole` elements with `shape: "oval"` when converting Circuit JSON into solver obstacles. As a result, a different-net pour could extend into the pad's required clearance. Same-net oval plated holes also lacked thermal-relief support.

This affected the oval battery pads on the ATTiny85 Arcade Keychain. Updating the shared dependency brings the fix to designs using the `tscircuit` package without requiring board-specific keepouts.

## What changed

Update `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` from `^0.0.51` to `^0.0.52` and refresh `bun.lock`. The release includes https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/pull/86, which preserves oval pad dimensions and rotation, offsets their elliptical geometry by the configured clearance, and supports thermal-relief spokes.

## Validation

- Both local smoke tests passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The full `bun test` run did not pass: the `published package does not depend on manifold-3d` audit timed out after 60 seconds during its clean npm installation.
- The solver change was separately validated with all 51 solver tests, TypeScript checks, and its production build.

title: fix: preserve C7519 schematic body fill and visible diodes
description: Fixes rendering of the C7519 schematic by preserving the fill color and visibility of protection diodes, correcting a bug where the fill color was incorrectly displayed as the outline color.
body: C7519 (USBLC6-2SC6) renders as a solid red rectangle, obscuring its internal protection-diode network. EasyEDA specifies a white body with a red outline, but the installed tscircuit `SchematicRect` implementation drops `fillColor` when emitting Circuit JSON, so the SVG renderer falls back to the outline color for the fill. Emit a closed `schematicpath` when a rectangle has different fill and outline colors. Paths preserve both colors, restoring C7519's white body and all five visible protection diodes while preserving its position, dimensions, and stroke width. Rectangles with no fill or matching fill and outline colors retain their existing primitive. Builds on the reproduction merged in #542. Updates its schematic snapshot and checks the white body, red outline, stroke width, and five filled diode paths. Adds coverage for unfilled and same-color rectangles, including their dimensions and six ports. Pin-label rendering and rounded corners are outside this fix. ## Before ## After Validation: - Focused symbol-generation and C7519 tests: 10 passed. - Compared generated TSX for all 92 saved EasyEDA part fixtures against clean main at `9af082d`: only C7519 changed; the other 91 outputs were identical, with no conversion errors. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run format:check`: passed. - Full `bun test`: 192 passed, 16 failed across 144 files. All 11 schematic snapshot failures also reproduce on clean main with the same installed dependencies (C1046, C18185602, C19076967, C281113, C2961147, C2998002, C309274, C8545, including the STEP-model and L0805 cases). All five timeout failures passed when rerun with CI's `--timeout 60000` (three C472489 cases, C46497, C60708). No unrelated snapshots were updated.

title: Disambiguate disconnected same-name nets with schematic superscripts
description: Populates display_superscript when a name is displayed on more than one source electrical network, ensuring disconnected GND nets in sibling subcircuits render as GND and GND, while connected copies share one suffix and unambiguous names have none.
body:
Populates `display_superscript` when a name is displayed on more than one source electrical network. Unused source-net declarations do not create display conflicts. For example, disconnected GND nets in sibling subcircuits render as GND¹ and GND². Connected copies share one suffix; unambiguous names have none.

Applies to both `schematic_net_label` and trace-associated `schematic_text`, including inline display labels that have no `source_net`. Connectivity follows source traces, shared ports, and both forms of internal component pin connections across subcircuits. Scoped connectivity keys and matching names alone do not join networks.

Runs in the dedicated `SchematicLabelNetsWithConflictingNames` render phase after schematic label/symbol rendering and before PCB phases. The top-level group assigns suffixes for the whole circuit, with initial and dirty-update handlers and declared async dependencies. Clears stale suffixes when networks join and uses source member IDs for deterministic numbering even when Circuit JSON is reordered. Source names, connectivity, and unrelated schematic text remain unchanged. Updates circuit-json to 0.0.484 and circuit-to-svg to 0.0.413, which contain the schema and rendering support.

![Core-generated GND and inline SIGNAL superscripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/feat/disambiguate-schematic-net-names/tests/features/schematic-net-superscripts/__snapshots__/disconnected-subcircuits-schematic.snap.svg)

Validation:
- Four new tests with visual snapshots cover disconnected and connected subcircuits, shared numbering between label kinds, inline named traces, internal connections, reordered JSON, and removal of stale suffixes.
- Existing trace/subcircuit/inline-label regression batch: 75 pass, one existing skip. Additional explicit-label and group-port batches: 11 pass and 6 pass.
- Phase lifecycle tests verify that assignment completes inside the phase, waits for descendant async label work, runs once initially, and reruns on dirty updates.
- The RP2040 regression verifies XIN remains unsuffixed despite duplicate source-net declarations; its schematic snapshot is updated.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` pass.

Related schema/rendering changes: tscircuit/circuit-json#750, tscircuit/circuit-json#754, tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#712.

title: Render superscripts on net labels and inline schematic text
description: Renders display_superscript on both schematic_net_label and schematic_text as a smaller raised suffix, supporting outlined labels in all orientations, groundpower symbols, and inline labels alongside wires.
body:
Renders `display_superscript` on both `schematic_net_label` and `schematic_text` as a smaller raised suffix. Supports outlined labels in all four orientations, ground/power symbols, and inline labels alongside wires. Label outlines and auto-fit bounds include the suffix. Omitted or empty suffixes preserve existing output.

This PR is also a visual proposal for deciding whether to proceed with net disambiguation. Columns below show no suffix, `1`, `2`, and `12`; rows show left/right/top/bottom outlined labels, ground symbols, and power symbols.

![Net label superscript comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/feat/net-label-display-superscript/docs/images/net-label-superscript.png)

Schema: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/750. A structural extension supports the optional field against the current dependency. This renderer does not assign suffixes or change net identity; the producer supplies `display_superscript`.

Related warning schema: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/749.

Validation: 102 schematic tests pass (one existing TODO); ESM and declaration build pass. Added a visual snapshot covering 24 labels, escaped suffix text, empty-suffix compatibility, multi-character width, and center-based auto-fit bounds in every orientation.

Full TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`) also passes.

Connectivity check: https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/264.

Inline net labels use `schematic_text`, with the schema added in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/754. Suffixes inherit color, scale with the font, respect anchoring and rotation, and append once to the final line of multiline text. Tests cover these behaviors, escaping, compatibility, and bounds for long suffixes.

![Inline net label superscripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/feat/net-label-display-superscript/docs/images/inline-net-label-superscript.png)

This keeps the earlier removal of `sheet_index` tiling; it only uses the explicit center when one is present.

title: Use inclusive via-span DRC and preserve staged repairs
description: Fixes via span DRC evaluation to include all layers in the reference DRC, ensuring accurate collision detection and preserving staged repairs during autorouting.
body:
Vias spanning multiple board layers were exported to reference DRC using only their two endpoint layers, hiding collisions on intermediate copper. Use the shared inclusive-span helper in the reference converter so it agrees with indexed DRC. Via inputs use required `from_layer` and `to_layer` endpoints exclusively; remove the optional `layers` override.

Pin `high-density-repair03` to `9d6da7d`, including the endpoint-only API in tscircuit/high-density-repair03#99 and staged repair selection in tscircuit/high-density-repair03#97. The latter allows a trace-clean layer move with residual via-pad issues to reach the following repair phase, while retaining via-trace and via-pair guards. Without it, the expanded checks exposed a five-error regression on SRJ18 sample 12.

Add indexed/reference span agreement and full sample-12 regressions. Enable Pipeline 7's via ownership metadata to match Pipeline 9, and update bugreport77's assertion and visual snapshot to verify fewer than its original 94 reference errors and zero via-related errors. Via generation is unchanged.

Validation on `8738842`: local typecheck/build and all three focused regressions pass, including sample 12 with zero DRC errors and bugreport77 with unchanged snapshots after the endpoint-only update. The shared dependency has 89 passing tests and green CI. All 13,995 committed JSON fixture vias already use both endpoints; none uses a `layers` override.

Fresh `/benchmark-all --same-machine` compares current main `fc0f633` with this PR `8738842`:

| Dataset | Completion, main → PR | DRC pass, main → PR | Issues, main → PR | Timeouts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dataset01 | 85/85 → 85/85 | 85/85 → 85/85 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| SRJ18 | 13/16 → 13/16 | 8/16 → 8/16 | 87 → 98 | 1 → 1 |

[Dataset01 results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33977792323), [SRJ18 results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33977793156). title: Improve Pipeline11 simplification with vertex shortcuts
description: Adds a collision-checked vertex cleanup pass to Pipeline11s path simplifier, reducing redundant vertices and improving route quality on the RP2040 motor controller.
body:
Pipeline11's sampled path simplifier leaves redundant vertices and short detours on the RP2040 motor controller. Add a collision-checked vertex cleanup pass after each path pass, searching farther route vertices within each anchored, constant-width layer section. Candidates must shorten the route or remove points at equal length. Terminal coordinates, layer transitions, through-obstacle segments, width changes, jumper anchors, and immutable peers remain protected.

On the RP2040 SRJ, compared with the previous Pipeline11 output:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Route points | 1,763 | 1,560 |
| Trace length | 1,496.99 mm | 1,492.37 mm |
| Traces | 148 | 148 |
| Vias | 73 | 73 |
| Relaxed DRC errors | 0 | 0 |

Enabled by default in Pipeline11, with `enableVertexShortcuts: false` retaining the previous algorithm for comparison. The additional collision search improves route quality at the cost of extra cleanup work; other pipelines retain their existing defaults.

The RP2040 test runs both configurations, asserts point/length improvements and DRC, and uses `stackSvgsHorizontally` from `stack-svgs` for the before/after SVG snapshot. Also updates the original board-input/output snapshot and adds focused clearance, anchor-preservation, and non-lengthening tests.
