title: Use endpoint pairs as the only via span API
description: Changes the via span API to exclusively use from_layer and to_layer, removing the optional layers field and ensuring DRC and Circuit JSON conversion derive the inclusive board-layer span from required endpoints.
body:
Use `from_layer` and `to_layer` as the sole via span API. Remove the optional via `layers` field and its precedence path; DRC and Circuit JSON conversion derive the inclusive board-layer span from required endpoints. Reversed endpoints produce the same geometry.

Replace explicit-layer tests with endpoint reversal and span-extension coverage, retaining intermediate-layer collisions, excluded layers, same-layer spans, and invalid endpoints. This is stacked on #97; merge that PR first.

Validation: all 89 tests pass (594 assertions) and typecheck passes. The autorouter consumer is updated in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2402.

title: Expand via-span DRC checks without routing changes
description: Normalizes DRC checks for vias to include all layers in their span, ensuring accurate collision detection across multiple layers without altering input geometry.
body:
Vias declared with `from_layer`/`to_layer` were checked only on their two endpoint layers, so a four-layer `top → inner2` via could intersect copper on `inner1` without a DRC error. Normalize the endpoint API to its inclusive board-layer span and use an explicit `layers` array directly when supplied.

The indexed DRC engine and circuit-json conversion share that normalization. HD conversion also uses the actual board layer count instead of assuming two layers. Added tests cover intermediate-layer trace and pad collisions, equivalent endpoint/array geometry, reversed and same-layer spans, invalid endpoints, and four-layer HD conversion. The checks leave input geometry unchanged.

This is the DRC-only portion of #95. It contains no solver or routing changes, no repair-stage scoring changes, no manufacturing-policy flag, no `addThroughViaLayersToTraces`, and no snapshot updates. Fixing the via-producing solvers, including investigating power-trace expansion, remains separate.

Validation: 88 local tests pass. The intermediate trace and pad collision reproductions both fail against the unchanged main DRC engine (it reports no collision), then pass with this change.

title: Fix DRC to check vias across their physical layer spans
description: Fixes DRC to ensure that vias are validated across their physical layer spans, preventing routing errors that could short copper on intermediate layers.
body:
Vias were indexed only on `from_layer` and `to_layer`, so repair could accept routes that shorted copper on intermediate layers or on other layers occupied by a through via. On a four-layer pedometer, a top→inner1 transition could therefore pass DRC while contacting a bottom-layer signal.

Resolve physical via layers once in a shared helper and use it in both `AutoroutingDrcEngine` and the Circuit JSON reference converter. Through vias occupy the full stack by default. When blind/buried vias are enabled, use the inclusive transition span or a validated explicit physical span. The converter also uses the actual board layer count for HD route coordinates.

Validation:
- 15 focused dependency tests pass, including intermediate-layer contact, through-via contact, positive insufficient clearance, via/pad and via/via interactions, same-net exemptions, and blind/buried spans.
- Consuming autorouter build (ESM and declarations) passes; its full pedometer regression changes from six via/trace violations with the unpatched engine to zero with this fix.
- Full CI tests, typecheck, and format check pass on the final commit. Local source/test typecheck also passes.

No benchmarks were run.

title: repro(svg): real board ignores active component display modes
description: Fixes the SVG renderer to correctly display active component display modes for polarized capacitors in schematics.
body: ## Problem The schematic SVG renderer ignores a component's active `DISPLAYMODE` when selecting component-owned primitives. In the power schematic used here, ten polarized capacitors have `DISPLAYMODE = 1`. Altium 365 renders their lower plates as curves, but altiumts renders the inactive mode-0 flat plates. ## Real-board reproduction This PR adds the unmodified, MIT-licensed [`AmirhosseinR/Altium_DSP_FPGA`](https://github.com/AmirhosseinR/Altium_DSP_FPGA) power schematic as a pinned reference: - commit: `61e66e61a6b7fbcfbc370a0b756b2958f38ad493` - SHA-256: `a0e51aeb708bcb7d8f444073a16e5edf9e8aee63ce28329122942ca27150373f` The original schematic naturally contains ten `Cap Pol3` components using display mode 1. Each contains mode-1 arc records for the curved polarized-capacitor plate. The test does not modify or crop the source schematic. It verifies those real binary records and records the current broken full-sheet SVG snapshot. ## Visual Comparison | altiumviewer.tscircuit.com | Reference (Altium 365) | | :---: | :---: | | | | ## Expected behavior The renderer should select each component's active display-mode primitives, producing curved lower plates for all ten polarized capacitors, matching Altium 365. Follow-up fix: #130

title: fix(site): enable vertical scrolling on left control panel
description: Fixes the inability to scroll vertically on the left control panel when content exceeds the viewport height on smaller screens.
body:
## Problem
On desktop and smaller laptop screens, the left `.control-panel` section cannot be scrolled vertically when content extends past the viewport height (e.g., on smaller displays, when error notices are displayed, or when download actions appear). This happened because `overflow: hidden;` was shared between `.control-panel` and `.viewer-panel`, clipping all overflowing content.

## Solution
- Removed `overflow: hidden;` from the shared `.control-panel, .viewer-panel` rule.
- Added `overflow-y: auto;`, `overflow-x: hidden;`, and `overscroll-behavior: contain;` specifically to `.control-panel`.
- Kept `overflow: hidden;` on `.viewer-panel` to preserve proper clipping for the preview frame's rounded corners.

## Verification
- Verified production site build via `bun run build:site`.
- Verified TypeScript checks via `bun run typecheck`.
- Formatted with Biome (`bun run format`).

body:
Add a deterministic PCB repro for false disconnected-endpoint errors where inner-layer traces meet separate same-net via-in-pad stubs.

The fixture models a 21 × 15 mm sensor-interface region with real IC, capacitor, and connector footprints. Ten 0.4/0.2 mm through-vias sit in the top-side pads, and separate inner-layer branches meet their copper. The SVG includes the checker’s actual error markers. This PR records the current erroneous result; the electrically connected endpoints should not be reported as floating.

This PR changes only the repro, its fixture, and its visual snapshot. It intentionally contains no checker fix. The follow-up fix is #269, stacked on this branch; it updates the same test and snapshot to the corrected result.

The baseline checker produces **eight false endpoint errors**, asserted by exact identity and position. The unmodified fixture produces zero with the fix. Error labels are abbreviated to E1–E8 for display only; the checked diagnostics retain their original contents.

Validation: **253 tests pass**, including this repro and snapshot; TypeScript and formatting pass. The fixture uses local generated footprints and explicit copper, with no autorouter or external lookup.

![Repro: eight false endpoint markers on a connected sensor PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/9de75cab8b0a14c23abcb91aa8415af10b645160/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-via-in-pad-net-contiguity.snap.svg)

description: Fixes false disconnected endpoints in the PCB checker when separate same-net vias are present, ensuring accurate connectivity reporting for net-level trace endpoints.
body:
Recognize separate same-net via copper when checking net-level trace endpoints. The realistic repro in [repro PR #270](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/270) has physically connected inner-layer branches, but the current checker reports their endpoints as disconnected because it only considers pads and lateral wire segments.

Index via copper by physical layer and require actual endpoint contact plus onward contact with a same-net pad or another trace. Explicit materialized via layers and dimensions take precedence over route-only data. Wrong nets, unsupported layers, gaps, a trace's own via, and lone vias still do not establish an onward connection. Existing missing-connection and other DRC checks remain intact.

This PR is stacked on [repro PR #270](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/270). Its snapshot change shows the same PCB geometry with the false markers removed. Merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to main.

The 21 × 15 mm sensor-interface fixture has a SOIC-8 IC, two 0603 decoupling capacitors, a four-pin connector, ten intentional through-vias, and separate inner-layer routes. The fixture is byte-identical across the two branches. The checker reports **eight false endpoints before, zero after**. E1–E8 are abbreviated display labels; assertions use the actual diagnostic IDs and positions.

Validation: **285 tests pass**, including 32 focused via regressions and the realistic snapshot repro; TypeScript and formatting pass. The pedometer integration still removes 48 false reports while retaining its five other errors. No routing or design-rule changes are part of this PR.

title: chore: update parts-engine to 0.0.31 for connector CAD sizing fix
description: Updates the parts-engine dependency to version 0.0.31 to include a CAD model sizing fix for JLCPCB components, ensuring accurate dimensions for USB-C connectors.
body:
Eval's default platform config uses Parts Engine to resolve and convert JLCPCB components. This raises `@tscircuit/parts-engine` from `^0.0.29` to `^0.0.31`, ensuring the minimum accepted release includes EasyEDA 0.0.350 and its CAD model sizing fix.

The fix was delivered through https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/51 and https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/pull/540. The converter previously mixed PCB footprint dimensions with an SVG height when setting `cad_component.size`. For C165948, this constrained the USB-C body to incorrect bounds and made it render too small relative to its footprint. With model bounds available, the converter now emits the model's own dimensions: **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**.

Eval explicitly bundles Parts Engine into its library, runner, webworker, and platform-config outputs. Updating EasyEDA in RunFrame or CLI alone does not replace the Parts Engine code in an already-built Eval release. Raising this dependency makes the corrected converter part of subsequent Eval builds, which downstream consumers must then adopt. This PR does not deploy the connector docs itself.

Only `package.json` changes; this repository does not track a lockfile.

Validation:
- Parts Engine/platform-config and JLCPCB footprint integration tests: **9 passed, 0 failed** across 5 files.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `bun run build:platform-config`: passed, including declaration generation.
- Called the default `getPlatformConfig().partsEngine.fetchPartCircuitJson` for C165948 and asserted the returned CAD dimensions are **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Selecting a phase displays its captured SRJ input or output in the real PCB viewer, preserving board context and camera position. ### Inspect in Cosmos

[Open the recorded PCB phase explorer](https://runframe-git-feat-autorouting-phase-explorer-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixtureId=%7B%22path%22%3A%22examples%2Fexample58-autorouting.fixture.tsx%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22Recorded%20sensor%20breakout%22%7D) · [Open the live RunFrame fixture](https://runframe-git-feat-autorouting-phase-explorer-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixtureId=%7B%22path%22%3A%22examples%2Fexample58-autorouting.fixture.tsx%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22Live%20sensor%20breakout%22%7D)

title: Prevent chip-anchored grounded load pair overlaps
description: Separates colliding chip-anchored grounded load pairs to prevent overlaps while preserving their vertical placement and ensuring valid pair placement.
body:
## Summary

- separate only colliding chip-anchored grounded load pairs
- move each resistor/load pair as one rigid unit while preserving its vertical placement
- use the existing chip gap and retain the collision group center
- leave already-clear branches unchanged
- strengthen the merged repro to require zero overlaps and valid pair placement

## Why

GroundedLoadPairSolver places each chip-anchored output branch independently, so nearby branches can occupy the same area. The fix groups only pairs that share a main chip and ground net, finds connected collision groups, and separates those groups horizontally without forcing every branch into a new row.

Embedded source escapes and adjacent narrow buses are ordered and reserved using their geometry, with package-edge via candidates available for pairs. The repair path also retains its validated reservations through subsequent routing.

title: fix: distinguish missing EasyEDA library entries from search failures
description: Fixes the distinction between missing EasyEDA library entries and search failures by validating search responses and providing contextual error messages.
body:
An empty EasyEDA library search and a rejected API request previously both reported `Component not found`; malformed decoded search responses could throw a property-access TypeError. For C41411351 this obscured the distinction between a real supplier catalog listing and an importable library component.

This fix builds on the regression tests merged in #548. It validates the search response before selecting an exact supplier match. Empty searches now identify the requested part and explain the library/catalog distinction; API rejections retain their code/message; malformed responses produce a contextual error before any geometry request. It also removes the untyped search-candidate callback. Exact matching, raw detail output and HTTP error handling are preserved.

Tests include the captured S4 response, 10 error snapshots, eight malformed/rejected-response cases, and all three existing supplier-identity fields. Success cases use a real diode fixture and verify unchanged raw output. Failure cases assert that no replacement component is fetched. No S4-specific production condition or alternative-footprint fallback is added.

Validation: the full suite passes (224 tests, 79 snapshots, 0 failures); formatting, TypeScript and build pass. Retargeted to `main` after #548 merged. The base update preserves the tested converter source and snapshots byte-for-byte and incorporates only the upstream package version bump. All 19 focused tests, 10 error snapshots, formatting and TypeScript checks pass again; all five GitHub checks pass on the updated head.

**S4 placement remains blocked by supplier content.** The exact standard product endpoint returned code 404, the supplier SVG viewer endpoint returned code 422 (`原理图未绘制`, schematic not drawn), and the Pro device lookup returned no entries on 2026-09-06. This fixes importer diagnostics and response validation; it does not supply a footprint, correct the reference circuit, or establish electrical verification. See [the S4 audit](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/Game-Boy-Enhance/tree/main/s4).

This PR does not unblock S4 placement. On 2026-09-06, the exact standard product endpoint returned code 404, the supplier SVG endpoint returned code 422 (`原理图未绘制`, schematic not drawn), and the Pro device lookup returned an empty list. No replacement footprint or board geometry is introduced.

## Summary

Adds a reproduction test (`repro182`) captured from Trellis Core (CPU Core sheet). 

When multiple decoupling capacitors for a large IC (such as `U3` / Allwinner T113-S3) are placed horizontally along power/ground rails (`P3V3`, `P0V9`, `P1V8`, `P1V5`, and `GND`), adjacent capacitors are paired and routed with trace lines rather than receiving clean, individual net labels or power/ground symbols.

### Current (Buggy) Behavior
Parallel decoupling capacitors connect to each other with horizontal traces (e.g. `C9.1 ↔ C10.1`, `C11.1 ↔ C12.1`, `C14.1 ↔ C15.1`), creating a fragmented/confusing trace routing across the bank rather than clean local net labels or dedicated rail symbols.

### Expected Behavior
Parallel decoupling capacitors on supply rails should either:
1. Each receive individual, clean local power (`P3V3`) and ground (`GND`) symbols/labels, OR
2. Consistently connect across continuous bus rails without arbitrary disjoint pairs.

## Changes
- Added `tests/repros/repro182-trellis-core-decoupling-snake-traces.test.tsx`:

## Summary

- add a responsive Related Packages section to the bottom of public package pages
- use the merged `/packages/list_related_packages` endpoint and render its thumbnail data
- render warm cached recommendations directly into the package-page SSR HTML for search crawlers
- seed React Query from the SSR payload so hydration does not issue a duplicate request
- retain the deferred browser fetch as the cold-cache fallback, which also populates the API cache on demand

## Performance

- begin the SSR `cached_only=true` request in parallel with existing package data fetching
- never wait for that request: use it only if it has settled by the time core SSR data is ready, otherwise abort it
- avoid database or similarity work on SSR cache misses
- keep API/browser results fresh for 48 hours
- lazy-load thumbnails with asynchronous decoding and low fetch priority
- silently omit the non-critical section if no cached result is ready and let the viewport-deferred client path fill it later

This gives warm-cache pages crawlable related-package links without adding the endpoint to the SSR critical path.

title: Fix bugreport94 HighDensity DRC without changing topology
description: Fixes bugreport94 by ensuring all 157 routes complete with zero physical DRC errors while maintaining the original topology construction.
body:
Bugreport94 now completes all 157 routes with zero physical DRC errors while keeping the original topology construction. The previous topology-compaction change and its unrelated snapshot changes have been removed; `pipeline7-full-pipeline-svg-frames.snap.svg` is identical to main.

The SRJ18 sample 3 regression came from giving repair candidate construction the original unexpanded pads in place of the processed routing obstacles. Keep the routing obstacles for candidate construction and use the original physical pads only in DRC evaluation.

Pin [high-density-repair03 PR #91](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/91) at `37d2b7af008c3a79c1a794e2ca307583a0f19c98`. Its repair includes the outgoing wire after a via, finds via placements that clear neighboring traces and pads across the full layer span, and checks newly introduced copper against the board outline. It uses existing geometry utilities and preserves pad dimensions and rotation.

For the remaining trace overlaps, reuse the existing regional HighDensity repair for mapped trace pairs within the existing post-exact precision limit. Normalize fixed-route net identities only in that temporary repair input, preserving initial routing and preloaded fanouts. After an accepted reroute, run one existing force-clearance pass on the resulting copper, accepting it only when DRC improves without adding via issues. This pass preserves route endpoints, layers, widths, and net identities. The original routing grid and search limit are unchanged.

Validation:

- Bugreport94: all 157 routes, zero physical DRC errors; strict regression assertion and actual output snapshots pass on both macOS and Linux (CI Bun 1.3.8).
- SRJ18 sample 3: zero relaxed DRC errors with a real-SRJ snapshot. Samples 5 and 9 also remain clear.
- Original Pipeline7 full-stage snapshot passes unchanged. Nine existing route-output snapshots were refreshed after checking that their pads, terminal points, and view bounds are unchanged; all 10 associated tests pass on both macOS and Linux. Bugreport90 uses the existing platform-specific snapshot convention with its original 1% tolerance.
- Existing regional search-limit and contiguous preload tests pass; the latest-main length-matching clearance test, preload-simplification tests, TypeScript, and production build also pass. The existing BGA route count, QFP one-via assertion, and SRJ18 sample 13 precision-limit assertions are unchanged and pass.
- HD CI tests, typecheck, and formatting pass on the pinned commit. [Final integration CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33995856556) passes on `e27f1c8b`: all nine test shards, build, TypeScript, formatting, ID checks, and deployment checks.
- Same-machine Dataset01 at `70284cdc` versus main `fb6c6d77`: 85/85 complete and 85/85 relaxed-DRC clean on both revisions, zero timeouts, and no per-board regressions. [Benchmark run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33995370787).

No board gains DRC errors; total errors decrease from 98 to 64. Sample 3 remains at zero errors. Median runtime is +2.5%, P95 +4.7%. [SRJ18 benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33995372134).

The benchmark revision is `70284cdc`; the final `e27f1c8b` follow-up changes only the existing bugreport90 test and its platform snapshots. Their production source and dependency pin are identical. title: Preserve connector orientation and detect beneficial QFN rotations
description: Preserve pin-header and connector orientation while detecting beneficial rotations for passives, crystals, diodes, and chips, retracting the J1 recommendation from 31 and extending the shared-net heuristic to multi-pin devices without legacy-specific chip exclusions.
body:
Preserve pin-header and connector orientation because their external pin order can be fixed, while detecting beneficial rotations for passives, crystals, diodes, and chips. This retracts the J1 recommendation introduced in #31 and extends the shared-net heuristic to multi-pin devices without legacy-specific chip exclusions.

For multi-pin components, compare each pin's nearest same-layer external destination with its position after a 180-degree rotation. Require every moving pin to favor the opposite orientation and get a shorter nearest-connection distance. Centered pads stay fixed and are excluded from the improvement requirement. Keep the existing two-pin centerline check. This conservative heuristic withholds a suggestion if any moving pin lacks a usable destination or fails to improve; it does not guarantee a shorter autorouted result.

The real-chip regression uses TI's DRV8833RTYR in WQFN-16, including its exposed ground pad and [datasheet pinout](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv8833.pdf). It is now a normal passing test: all 16 perimeter-pin distances improve, the center pad stays fixed, the original gets `rotate U1 180 degrees`, and the warning clears after rotation. A mixed case where one pin is already aligned produces no warning. The single-circuit SVG now shows the detected suggestion in blue. The fixture uses nominal QFN geometry and test points as external destinations; it is a placement test, not a functional motor-driver board.

The passive/crystal/diode cases retain their individual SVGs and before/after assertions. The J1 regression confirms the interface is preserved. Validation: all 16 tests, typecheck, and build pass locally; SVG inspected visually. No README changes.

Rotated pads were checked as axis-aligned copper, and some repair candidates moved a via away from one trace into another. The route converter also skipped the outgoing wire immediately after a via, so that copper was missing from the DRC input. The repair does not change obstacle approximations or topology construction. The repair now checks both wires adjoining a via and considers the clearance boundaries of neighboring traces when moving it. Pad checks cover every layer traversed by the via. Existing local displacement candidates remain available when unrelated DRC errors are present, within the same candidate limit. Newly introduced wires and vias must also respect the board outline. Terminal escape candidates retain the existing selection order and full-board DRC acceptance. This PR is based on [tests-only PR #98](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/98), stacked on [the upstream stage-handoff fix #97](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/97). The checker now measures those outlines correctly. Validation at `37d2b7af008c3a79c1a794e2ca307583a0f19c98`: - All 91 tests and TypeScript pass locally on macOS and Linux. title: fix(svg): paint transparent component fills first
description: Fixes rendering order of transparent component fills to ensure they are painted behind opaque symbol graphics in Altium schematics.

title: Fix child cadmodel rotation and size parity
description: Fixes child cadmodel elements to ensure correct rotation and size parity with the object-form cadModel API by removing an erroneous Z-axis rotation and preserving authored sizes in millimeters.
body:
## Summary

Make child `<cadmodel>` elements agree with the object-form `cadModel` API:

- Remove the extra bottom-layer Z half-turn. The existing Y=180 rotation already performs the layer flip; adding Z=180 changes which in-plane axis is reversed.
- Normalize emitted Z with the existing `normalizeDegrees` helper.
- Preserve authored `size` in `cad_component`, converting unit-bearing distances to millimeters.

This is independent of the enclosure/mounting-hardware work. The branch starts at upstream `main` (`1fc6c2c4`) and changes only `CadModel.ts` and two standalone regression files. No new dependencies or local package links.

## Test-first commit stack

1. `176a8fcd` — regression tests only, intentionally failing on upstream code.
2. `2ebeb3bd` — the fixes, with the same tests passing.

Command run before and after the fix:

```sh
bun test \
  ./tests/components/primitive-components/cadmodel-bottom-layer-rotation.test.tsx \
  ./tests/components/primitive-components/cadmodel-size.test.tsx
```

Observed failures before the fix:

```text
Bottom-layer rotation: expected 0, received 180
Authored size: expected { x: 6, y: 4, z: 20 }, received undefined
0 pass, 2 fail
```

The rotation assertion normalizes both positive and negative angle representations, so its failure isolates the erroneous half-turn rather than canonicalization. It covers both layers, all four right-angle placements, and additional authored rotation offsets.

The size regression covers numeric dimensions, SI-unit strings, and omission. Both regressions inspect emitted Circuit JSON from child and object-form CAD declarations and use only the existing upstream fixture infrastructure.

## Validation

- Both new regressions and adjacent CAD primitive tests: **8 passed, 0 failed**.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Biome formatting for changed files.
- `bun run build` and `bun run smoke-test:dist`

title: repro: polygon SMT pads receive zero copper-pour clearance
description: Reproduces a bug where polygon SMT pads receive zero copper-pour clearance, while rectangular pads receive the expected margin.
body:
With `<copperpour connectsTo="net.GND" layer="top" padMargin="0.5mm" />`, a polygon SMT pad on a different net receives no clearance: the GND pour reaches the signal-pad boundary. An identical square declared as `shape="rect"` receives the requested margin.

This is a reproduction-only PR in core: one test and its real PCB snapshot, rendered from the emitted Circuit JSON. No core implementation, solver, or dependency changes.

The fixture has two 2 × 2 mm square pads, one rectangular and one polygonal, on separate signal nets. Routing is disabled to isolate pad clearance. The test measures all four side gaps from the emitted pad geometry and the pour's BRep voids:

| Pad representation | Requested margin | Observed gap on each side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rect` | 0.5 mm | 0.5 mm |
| `polygon` | 0.5 mm | 0 mm |

The assertions and snapshot intentionally record the current bug so this reproduction can merge independently. A subsequent fix should change the polygon expectation to 0.5 mm and update this same snapshot, producing a visible image diff.

![Actual PCB snapshot: rectangular pad has a clearance gap, polygon pad touches the GND pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/73f6225e292ac0149b7d89eb9676cf6f879bd731/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-polygon-pad-copper-pour-clearance-pcb.snap.svg)

Confirmed on core `54ff0d19ce160c67528b6e3c6efdfe0dd49ce8a5` (0.0.1866) with its installed `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` 0.0.52. Core passes `padMargin` through as `pad_margin`; the dependency's `lib/solvers/copper-pour/process-obstacles.ts` polygon-pad branch calls `getMargin(0)`, while the rectangle branch calls `getMargin(padMargin)`. This documents the behavior of these versions, not a claim about every later solver revision.

Validation with Bun 1.4.0:
- `bun test tests/repros/repro-polygon-pad-copper-pour-clearance.test.tsx`: passes.
- The reproduction plus related copper-pour and polygon-pad tests: 22 pass, 0 fail.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passes.
- Biome formatting check for the new test: passes.
- Temporarily changing the installed solver's polygon margin to `getMargin(padMargin)` causes the snapshot to fail (1.96% pixel difference). The dependency was restored byte-for-byte and the reproduction passed again; that diagnostic change is not included in this PR.

title: fix: synchronize every branch of a shared fanout exit
description: Fixes the synchronization issue of shared capacitor pads in PCB routing, ensuring all branches correctly reference the relocated fanout exit.
body:
## Stack: 2 of 2

Depends on #3707. This PR is based on `codex/repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff`, so its diff contains only the fix, strengthened assertions, and the before/after PCB snapshot change. Merge #3707 first, then retarget this PR to main.

## Cause and fix

A real capacitor pad can be shared by multiple external source traces. Native fanout relocates the common breakout endpoint, but `Group_syncFanoutExitsWithGlobalConnections` uses `.find()` and updates only the first matching global connection. Later routing phases inherit the old coordinates for the other branches despite carrying the same physical point identity.

Collect all matching downstream endpoint references before changing their coordinates, then synchronize every reference. Retain the existing source-trace/endpoint identity guards and routing-group exclusion. Preserve each point's identity and unrelated metadata, while replacing position/layer and clearing obsolete layer/terminal-via overrides exactly as for the original first branch. No router or dependency changes.

## Real circuit regression

J1 supplies VCC/GND to a 100 nF 0402 capacitor and a parallel 10 kΩ 0402 load. Both capacitor pads have two real external branches. Native breakout/fanout and the default Pipeline 9 autorouter generate all copper; no mocked solvers, artificial SRJ inputs, manual copper, database injections, or disabled checks.

The updated test verifies both branches use each moved endpoint, emitted copper meets each handoff, external component pads remain unchanged, and the final circuit plus routing/placement checks contain no errors. Against unpatched core, the corrected assertion fails because the supply-load endpoint remains at (-0.55, -3.2999) instead of the actual fanout exit (-1.5, 0).

### Before

![Baseline: dangling capacitor handoffs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/4de10c0b80c2c017f37d67ddd5c797f69761915a/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff-pcb.snap.svg)

### After

![Fixed: both capacitor branches connected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/b0a08fad7c9a634d43ec84da81336f51456db16d/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff-pcb.snap.svg)

## Validation

- New repro: `bun test tests/repros/repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff.test.tsx` passes repeatedly without updating snapshots (23 assertions).
- `runAllRoutingChecks`, `runAllPlacementChecks`, and circuit error records are empty for the fixed repro.
- Eight focused existing tests pass: nested/manual breakouts, SOT23 power rail, QFP16, compacted-net handoff, SII9022 HDMI handoff, and plane fanout. Existing snapshots unchanged.
- Full `bun test tests/breakout --timeout 120000`: 21 pass, 2 existing skips, 1 pre-existing SOIC8 autorouting-SRJ snapshot mismatch (0.10%). Reproduced on unpatched 4de10c0b80c2c017f37d67ddd5c797f69761915a with identical dependencies; baseline and patched diff PNGs are byte-identical. Its snapshot is intentionally unchanged.
- `bun run build` passes.
- `node --max-old-space-size=6144 node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` passes. The default 2 GB Node heap exhausted memory on the full typecheck.
- Targeted Biome formatting check and `git diff --check` pass.
- Both PCB SVGs were rendered and visually inspected.

This fixes the shared-breakout handoff defect; it does not claim the larger Linux board or separate router issues are resolved.

title: repro: snapshot shared capacitor breakout handoff gaps
description: Reproduces a bug where shared capacitor breakout points lead to dangling copper connections in PCB routing, with a comprehensive test to validate the issue.
body:
## Stack: 1 of 2 — snapshot repro only

Adds a real routed TSX circuit and its PCB SVG snapshot, with no production-code changes. The follow-up fix is #3708, based on this branch so reviewers can see the actual copper diff.

J1 is a two-pin VCC/GND input. C1 is a 100 nF 0402 decoupling capacitor and R1 is a 10 kΩ 0402 load connected across those rails. Each capacitor pad participates in two distinct external source traces. The native breakout solver generates the boundary points; native fanout moves them, then the default Pipeline 9 autorouter routes the external branches in successive phases.

There are no mocked solvers, hand-authored SRJ inputs, injected PCB records, manual traces, or disabled DRC checks.

### What this reproduces

Core synchronizes only the first global connection referencing each moved capacitor breakout point. The later load branch retains the original boundary coordinates, leaving visible dangling copper. The completed baseline render reports three missing-connection errors.

This first test intentionally records the known-broken behavior: the first branch moves, the second stays at the old endpoint, and the PCB SVG shows the resulting gaps. It also verifies that the traces genuinely share a C1 port and that external component pads are unchanged. The stacked fix replaces those known-bad expectations with continuity and zero-error assertions.

### Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff.test.tsx` — passes against the broken baseline (19 assertions).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — passes on the repro branch.
- SVG rendered and visually inspected; snapshot text states the expected electrical connectivity.

Merge this repro before the stacked fix.

description: Fixes the issue where EXSW1s mounting pads disappear from the SRJ due to the getObstaclesFromCircuitJson function not handling specific shapes correctly.
body:
EXSW1's mounting pads disappear from the SRJ because `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` does not handle `pill_hole_with_rect_pad` or `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad`.

Convert both shapes into rectangular obstacles using the copper pad's center, dimensions, and rotation. Reuse quarter-turn normalization and preserve plated-hole metadata, connectivity, and all board layers.

Follow-up to #3703, which should merge first. Changes its `test.failing` back to plain `test`: each of EXSW1's two mounting pad IDs must now appear in the SRJ obstacles. No snapshots.

Validation: the focused test passes with the fix and plain `test`; on the repro branch it passes under `test.failing` because the pads are absent. The implementation also passed 50 targeted tests, typecheck, and build during initial validation. The full keyboard was not rerouted.

title: repro: panel export discards individual board profiles and connector notches
description: Reproduces a bug where adding a panel replaces individual board profiles with a bounding rectangle and removes connector notches during Gerber export.
body:
Adding `pcb_panel` to an input with two board profiles replaces both profiles with the panel's bounding rectangle on `Edge_Cuts`. The connector notch in the left board's outline disappears too. Removing only the panel element restores both profiles.

This is a reproduction only: a small typed fixture, assertions documenting the observed output, and real top/bottom Gerber export snapshots with and without the panel. No exporter code changes. Run `bun test tests/gerber/panel-board-outlines-repro.test.ts`.

Confirmed on upstream `1818400fca4a89f7805c34a851eb14c3168da332` (0.0.104). The board-edge skip was intentional in #65 and #75 for panels whose routing cutouts leave holding tabs. This demonstrates the missing individual-board export path; it does not imply that complete board outlines should be added to every tabbed panel. The separate fix is #167, which provides that path explicitly.

Validation: `bun test` (114 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, and `bun run format:check` (passes with the existing oversized-fixture warning).

Visual explanation (display strokes enlarged for readability):

![Without the panel both profiles are present; with the panel only the outer rectangle is exported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/e2337a5f80387f0c8d5fdc7b47dd77b2e37499c0/docs/images/panel-board-outlines-repro.png)

These labeled images are explanatory documentation. The tests use the repository’s standard `toMatchGerberSnapshot` matcher on the complete `convertCircuitJsonToGerberFiles` output, producing actual top and bottom Gerber stackup snapshots. Test rendering has no custom comparison layout or enlarged strokes. The fixture contains only board/panel geometry, so the real renders show bare board profiles.

title: fix: use explicit via endpoints in Pipeline9 copper validation
description: Fixes autorouting failure by interpreting diagonal layer transitions using explicit via endpoints in Pipeline9 copper validation, ensuring successful routing and validation of connections.
body:
## Stack

Based on #2453, which contains the real TSX circuit and baseline PCB snapshot.

## Fix

Interpret diagonal layer transitions using the solver's explicit via endpoint,
consistently with route materialization. Preserve per-point widths, colocated
transitions, through-obstacle handling, and input immutability.

## Real-world before/after

The regression freshly renders a complete T113-S3 footprint, a 3.3 kΩ boot
pulldown, five 0402 SD resistors, and a real bottom-layer GND pour. Native
Pipeline 9 and FanoutSolver generate all preloaded copper during the test.

With the same inputs, the baseline fails final regional-candidate validation.
This fix routes all seven connections, moving the actual ground escape to make
room for the five SD connections. The changed PCB SVG is the unmodified output
of `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` using default rendering options, the actual TSX
components, and native solver copper. There are no custom SVG elements, captions,
crops, zooms, or color overrides.

The fixed test asserts:

- Successful native routing with seven output traces.
- Zero native relaxed DRC errors with all original connection metadata retained;
  no continuity or clearance errors are filtered.
- A single 0.55/0.30 mm top-to-bottom via connected to the rendered GND pour.
- At least 0.10 mm clearance to every foreign-net pad.

## Validation

- Real-circuit regression: 174 assertions pass locally.
- Six focused geometry regressions: 65 assertions pass locally.
- Default-heap full TypeScript check: passes.
- Production build: passes.

Both confirmed CI failures are corrected:

- The fixture loads native core from the complete pinned tscircuit runtime's
  compatible dependency context. No dependency symlinks or global overrides;
  old core/React/checks/circuit-json versions remain unchanged.
- The existing immutable-preload fixture now declares its already-expected via
  at `(2, 1)`. All route geometry, assertions, and strict validation are preserved.

After a fresh Bun 1.3.8 dependency install, host Bun 1.2.21 passes the real-circuit
snapshot, six geometry tests, corrected fixture, and two old core tests: 10 tests,
255 assertions. Another 23 preload/clearance/regional regressions pass (585
assertions). Full typecheck and build also pass; no SVG snapshots were changed.
Bun 1.3.8 on macOS crashes in its Wasm worker's libmalloc/pthread cleanup. The
current revision passes all nine Linux/Bun 1.3.8 CI shards. Logs confirm that
both the fixed native TSX circuit/snapshot and the corrected explicit-via fixture
pass. No pending or failing current-head checks remain.

This does not certify the full Linux board or its fabrication exports.

title: Reproduce Pipeline9 boot fanout failure with a real T113-S3 circuit
description: Reproduces a routing regression failure in the Pipeline9 autorouting system using a real T113-S3 circuit, enabling easier debugging and resolution of the issue.
body:
## Stack

First PR: real-circuit reproduction. Fix: #2455 (based on this branch).

## What changed

Replaced the captured-candidate geometry diagram with a freshly rendered TSX
component-to-component circuit on every test run:

- Complete 129-pad T113-S3 footprint, one 3.3 kΩ boot resistor, and five 0402 SD
  interface resistors; 141 real pads total.
- Native bottom-layer GND pour.
- Pipeline 9 routes the boot signal, the native fanout solver generates its
  ground escape, and Pipeline 9 then routes the five SD connections using only
  those real native preloads.
- No recorded candidate, hand-written copper, fake solver result, or validation
  callback replacement.

The test records the existing real routing failure after the boot stage. Its PCB
SVG is the unmodified output of `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg`, with default
rendering options, actual TSX component footprints, and native solver copper.
There are no custom SVG elements, captions, crops, zooms, or color overrides.
#2455 changes the snapshot to the completed routed circuit with native DRC checks.

Newer rendering/fanout dependencies are pinned test-only aliases. A small
Bun-native runtime import boundary and scoped JSX declaration isolate their
dependencies and type definitions from the repository's older core tests. The
exports are the genuine native core implementations, not wrappers or mocks.

## Validation

- Focused regression: passes on the repro branch, asserting the native failure.
- Full default-heap TypeScript check: passes.
- Production build: passes.

The clean-install dependency failure is corrected: the fixture now depends on
the complete pinned `tscircuit@0.0.2467` runtime, which supplies compatible
versions of core's wildcard peers. Bun resolves its native core directly in that
dependency context, without importing unrelated eval/CLI exports. Existing root
core, React, circuit-json, and checks versions remain unchanged.

Verified with a fresh Bun 1.3.8 dependency install, no local dependency symlinks:
the repro and unchanged PCB snapshot pass under host Bun 1.2.21, as do the older
core tests, full typecheck, and build. Bun 1.3.8 on macOS crashes in its Wasm
worker's libmalloc/pthread cleanup. On the current revision, Linux/Bun 1.3.8 CI
passes all nine test shards, including the real TSX circuit and unchanged PCB
snapshot. All 14 active GitHub Actions checks are green, including formatting,
typecheck, builds, and source-policy checks.

This is a routing regression circuit, not certification of the full Linux board
or its manufacturing outputs.

title: Raise SRJ18 DRC passes to 62.5% with a uniform bounded pipeline
description: Pipeline9 leaves repairable clearance violations after its main repair portfolio. This PR raises SRJ18 DRC passes from 816 (50) to 1016 (62.5), with no lost passes. Runtime on the 12 boards completed by both revisions increases 2.62; P90 improves 4.81, and timeouts fall from two to one. Joint repair now follows one sequence: GlobalDrcBranchPortfolioSolver  clearance adjustment  terminal relocation  existing regional B01 repair  bounded Repair04 regions. Already-clean results stop early. The solver uses its concrete class type; the adaptive probe, structural solver intersection, and DRC-count-based stage gates are removed. Work limits apply to candidate evaluations and search nodes directly. Clearance adjustment tries at most 24 candidates across eight passes. Original failing contacts must exceed their configured clearance by 0.010 mm, and the complete board must pass reference DRC, including continuity, before these changes are published. Unsupported measurements have an explicit typed result. Terminal relocation uses original physical pad dimensions and rotation, keeping endpoints inside the original physical copper. A global budget allows at most 256 candidate evaluations across all contacts and passes. Repair04 tries 10 mm and 16 mm contexts with shared limits of four region calls, 1,024 candidate attempts, and 480,000 path-search nodes. Candidates must reduce full-board reference errors, preserve fixed copper, and introduce no new viapad violations. Intermediate regional improvements remain private unless full reference DRC passes. Its physical support constraints for preloaded copper and safety collars are retained. Repair04 is pinned to 79f794a426c32740ad89edf3624ac9e0c881bc13 and bundled. Checker versions, benchmark settings, trace widths, and via diameters are unchanged.  Same-machine results Both datasets compare 13f26bd2 against main 3d42af76, sequentially on the same 8-vCPU Linux ARM Blacksmith runner per dataset. Current head b60b5aa8 differs only in a regression-test assertion; its production, dependency, and benchmark code is identical to the measured revision. Negative timing deltas are faster.  Dataset  DRC passes  Timeouts  Shared completed runtime  P50  P90  P95   ---  ---  ---  ---:  ---:  ---:  ---:   SRJ18(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2442issuecomment-5575221470)  8  10 of 16  2  1  2.62  4.04  4.81  4.13   Dataset01(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2442issuecomment-5575221613)  85  85 of 85  0  0  2.70  7.81  9.39  7.43  SRJ18 samples 4 and 8 become DRC-clean. Sample 2 changes from a timeout to a completed route with seven remaining DRC issues. Sample 6 still times out; samples 14 and 15 retain their pathing failures. On the shared 12 completed boards, DRC issues fall 57  44 and vias fall 2,251  2,246. Nine output SVGs are byte-identical; only samples 4, 8, and 13 change. Sample 4 removes six vias. Sample 13 fixes five more issues (45  40), adds one via (230  231), and takes 273.61  304.16 seconds (11.16). This is the main per-board performance cost of applying the bounded stages uniformly. Shared completed runtime is 1,516.27  1,555.95 seconds (2.62). Summed runtime across all 16 samples is 2,453.00  2,491.37 seconds (1.56). The reports raw DRC total is 57  51 and its average-via metric rises because the PR additionally completes sample 2 with seven issues and 496 vias; these totals compare different completed cohorts. body:
Pipeline9 leaves repairable clearance violations after its main repair portfolio. This PR raises SRJ18 DRC passes from **8/16 (50%) to 10/16 (62.5%)**, with no lost passes. Runtime on the 12 boards completed by both revisions increases **2.62%**; P90 improves **4.81%**, and timeouts fall from two to one.

Joint repair now follows one sequence: `GlobalDrcBranchPortfolioSolver` → clearance adjustment → terminal relocation → existing regional B01 repair → bounded Repair04 regions. Already-clean results stop early. The solver uses its concrete class type; the adaptive probe, structural solver intersection, and DRC-count-based stage gates are removed. Work limits apply to candidate evaluations and search nodes directly.

- Clearance adjustment tries at most 24 candidates across eight passes. Original failing contacts must exceed their configured clearance by 0.010 mm, and the complete board must pass reference DRC, including continuity, before these changes are published. Unsupported measurements have an explicit typed result.
- Terminal relocation uses original physical pad dimensions and rotation, keeping endpoints inside the original physical copper. A global budget allows at most 256 candidate evaluations across all contacts and passes.
- Repair04 tries 10 mm and 16 mm contexts with shared limits of four region calls, 1,024 candidate attempts, and 480,000 path-search nodes. Candidates must reduce full-board reference errors, preserve fixed copper, and introduce no new via/pad violations. Intermediate regional improvements remain private unless full reference DRC passes. Its physical support constraints for preloaded copper and safety collars are retained.

Repair04 is pinned to `79f794a426c32740ad89edf3624ac9e0c881bc13` and bundled. Checker versions, benchmark settings, trace widths, and via diameters are unchanged.

### Same-machine results

Both datasets compare `13f26bd2` against main `3d42af76`, sequentially on the same 8-vCPU Linux ARM Blacksmith runner per dataset. Current head `b60b5aa8` differs only in a regression-test assertion; its production, dependency, and benchmark code is identical to the measured revision. Negative timing deltas are faster.

| Dataset | DRC passes | Timeouts | Shared completed runtime | P50 | P90 | P95 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2442#issuecomment-5575221470) | 8 → 10 of 16 | 2 → 1 | +2.62% | +4.04% | −4.81% | −4.13% |
| [Dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2442#issuecomment-5575221613) | 85 → 85 of 85 | 0 → 0 | −2.70% | −7.81% | +9.39% | −7.43% |

SRJ18 samples 4 and 8 become DRC-clean. Sample 2 changes from a timeout to a completed route with seven remaining DRC issues. Sample 6 still times out; samples 14 and 15 retain their pathing failures.

On the shared 12 completed boards, DRC issues fall **57 → 44** and vias fall **2,251 → 2,246**. Nine output SVGs are byte-identical; only samples 4, 8, and 13 change. Sample 4 removes six vias. Sample 13 fixes five more issues (45 → 40), adds one via (230 → 231), and takes **273.61 → 304.16 seconds (+11.16%)**. This is the main per-board performance cost of applying the bounded stages uniformly.

Shared completed runtime is **1,516.27 → 1,555.95 seconds (+2.62%)**. Summed runtime across all 16 samples is **2,453.00 → 2,491.37 seconds (+1.56%)**. The report's raw DRC total is 57 → 51 and its average-via metric rises because the PR additionally completes sample 2 with seven issues and 496 vias; these totals compare different completed cohorts.

Dataset01 retains 85/85 DRC passes and 3,189 vias. Summed runtime is **349.85 → 340.42 seconds (−2.70%)**. 84/85 SVGs are byte-identical. Sample 63 remains clean with the same widths, layers, and via count; one via moves 0.002 mm and wire length increases 0.117 mm (0.057%). Timing percentiles vary as shown above; these are paired-run measurements, not a claim that every board gets faster.

### Validation

- 17 focused tests pass with 626 assertions. New regressions cover more than eight real contacts, translated and rotated geometry, full reference DRC, endpoints, copper dimensions, unsupported identity, and global work caps.
- Full SRJ18 samples 4/8/9/13 and partially routed SRJ23 samples 50/52 pass locally. Linux ARM/Bun 1.4.2 also passes sample 4 and precision regressions.
- Typecheck and package build pass locally. Final-head CI build, typecheck, formatting, no-ID-hacks, Vercel checks, and [all nine test shards](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/34158728435) pass.

title: Deduplicate concurrent JLC part lookups
description: Deduplicates concurrent JLC part lookups to prevent multiple identical requests from being sent, improving efficiency and reducing HTTP 429 errors.
body:
Rendering many repeated components can start the same JLC search once per component before the first response populates the cache. The reported keyboard package has 87 automatic lookups, including 68 identical 100 nF 0402 capacitor lookups, and 82 of those requests received HTTP 429 responses.

Store each pending lookup before awaiting the response so concurrent callers share one request. Remove the pending entry in `finally`, allowing a transient network failure to be retried, while keeping the existing resolved-response cache behavior.

This complements #54 (category-safe cache keys) and #55 (rejecting HTTP error responses); neither currently coalesces in-flight requests.

Validation:

- `bun test` — 37 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

Reproduction discussion: https://community.tscircuit.com/thread/1546499364065902662

title: repro: battery charger status LED auto-layout causes U1 and R_CHG component overlap
description: Fixes overlap issue between resistor R_CHG and main IC U1 in battery charger status LED layout due to lack of collision detection in auto-layout algorithm.
body:
## Summary
Adds a layout reproduction test captured from `@tscircuit/core` where `AlignChipConnectedRailLoadsSolver` causes resistor `R_CHG` to overlap main IC `U1`.

## Problem
When aligning rail-connected load pairs (active-low status LEDs and current-limiting resistors) connected across multiple sides of a chip, `alignChipConnectedRailLoads` applies a rigid horizontal shift across all pairs without collision detection, placing `R_CHG` directly on top of `U1` (overlap area: 0.4080).

## Verification

- `bun run format:check` (clean)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` (clean)

title: Keep eligible labels inline with local trace shifts
description: Eligible endpoints could fall back to anchored labels when another endpoint on the same net was obstructed. Nearby routed wires could also cross inline text or terminal wires. Keep fallback local to each connected component and replace routed components atomically. Preserve the existing preferredopposite-side search, fitting full-size text into available wire gaps before flipping. Use small sideways shifts of existing rails and nearby power connectors; reject added bends, new crossings, disconnected junctions, and pin-clearance violations. Connector IDs flow from their producer. Collision records use exact identities instead of parsing ID prefixes or delimiter-based keys. Refinement advances through step() and activeSubSolver, preserves proposal ordering, and rejects failed candidates. The unchanged 1082 input produces 83 inline placements with no detected label or terminal-wire collisions. Fixture data and inline opt-in flags are unchanged. Three small snapshot updates remove text drawn twice at identical positions. Validation: 343 tests passed, 4 existing skips; typecheck, build, and formatting pass. The identityrefinement refactor changed no snapshot files; traces and label placements are identical across 27 audited fixtures. C3 and TIDA snapshots match main.

title: fix: include pill rectangular pads in copper pour obstacles
description: Fixes copper pours overlapping plated holes by including pill rectangular pads in the conversion process, ensuring proper respect for pad dimensions, position, rotation, and clearance.
body:
Copper pours overlap plated holes with `pill_hole_with_rect_pad` and `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad` because the Circuit JSON converter omits both shapes. Include them in the existing rectangular-pad conversion so pours respect the pad dimensions, position, rotation, layer, and configured clearance.

The unrotated shape uses zero rotation; the rotated shape uses `rect_ccw_rotation`, independently of the drill rotation. Both retain the existing connectivity lookup and plated-hole flag.

Adds 10 regression cases covering top and bottom layers at 0°, 45°, 90°, 180°, and 270°. Tests check the converted obstacles and emitted clearance geometry, including an offset drill with a different rotation from its pad.

Reproduction in core: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3748. Core will need a solver dependency update and updated reproduction expectations after this fix is released.

Validation:
- Before the fix: all 10 new regression cases failed with an empty pad array.
- After the fix: full `bun test` suite passed (69 tests).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` passed.
- Changed files formatted with Biome; `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix: respect copper-pour clearance around polygon pads
description: Fixes copper-pour clearance issue for polygon SMT pads on different nets, ensuring nonzero pad margins are respected.
body:
Polygon SMT pads on a different net currently get zero copper-pour clearance even when a nonzero pad margin is configured. This fixes the behavior reproduced in [tscircuit/core#3747](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3747).

Change the polygon-pad obstacle branch from `getMargin(0)` to `getMargin(padMargin)`. It now uses the existing polygon-offset path with the requested clearance, just like other pad shapes. The existing `getMargin` rules still preserve cutout/hole margins and zero additional keepout margin; same-net pads retain their existing direct/thermal connection behavior.

Actual PCB snapshots, with identical 2 × 2 mm rectangular and polygonal signal pads in a GND pour requesting 0.5 mm clearance:

| Before: core reproduction | After: corrected solver |
| --- | --- |
| ![Polygon signal pad touching the GND pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/73f6225e292ac0149b7d89eb9676cf6f879bd731/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-polygon-pad-copper-pour-clearance-pcb.snap.svg) | ![Both signal pads have 0.5 mm clearance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/a091a986f0f646fd75bb8e7cb652c0f8a500889d/tests/__snapshots__/polygon-pad-margin.snap.svg) |

Add geometry regression coverage for 0, 0.2, and 0.5 mm pad margins, hole/cutout/keepout margin rules, and same-net direct connections. The visual test renders the solver under test rather than core's bundled solver. Update the existing STM32F746G-DISCO top snapshot where polygon obstacles now gain clearance; its bottom snapshot is unchanged.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 59 pass, 0 fail; the two nonzero-margin geometry cases fail before the implementation change.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and `bun run format:check`: pass (format check reports the existing oversized-fixture warnings).
- Core integration with Bun 1.4.0: temporarily load this built solver into the core reproduction and change its polygon expectation from `[0, 0, 0, 0]` to `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]`. The test passes with the updated PCB snapshot. Core's test, snapshot, and installed dependency were restored afterward; this PR changes the solver repository only.

title: Analyze two-pin component orientation
description: Adds an analyzer that recommends a 180 rotation for two-pin components facing away from a connected chip to reduce wire bends, excluding power or ground connections.
body:
Two-pin components facing away from a connected chip can cause avoidable wire bends. Add an analyzer that recommends a 180° rotation when it reduces those bends, including the wireless-mouse sensor's SPI MOSI and SCLK series resistors.

Exclude components when either pin is electrically connected to power or ground. Resolve connections using source traces, internal connections, and connectivity keys, and classify rails from explicit source-net or source-pin metadata. This applies to any component type without matching component names, net names, or fixed pin numbers.

The power/ground fixtures use native tscircuit JSX traces for both chip connections and net.GND/net.VCC connections. Each snapshot shows one circuit. Regression checks cover both component types and pins, power/ground metadata, net aliases, and signal controls using the same routed geometry.

Validation: 40 tests pass; typecheck and formatting pass. Unrelated snapshots are unchanged.

title: Add schematic text clearance and reset network grouping analyzers
description: Implements two analyzers for independent text clearance and reset network grouping in schematic analysis.
body:
Implements two analyzers from #46:

- **Independent text clearance:** reports annotations/headings crossing wires, component bounds or other independent text. Component reference/value labels such as U3 are excluded; moving them requires moving the component.
- **Reset-network grouping:** identifies a scattered reset pull-up/capacitor network. Respects separate groups/sheets and ambiguous hosts; a remote test point alone is not an error.

Reuses the merged TSX repros. No new test files or added fixtures. Validation: 47 tests pass (including the existing expected-failure cases), typecheck and formatting pass. Text bounds and reset distance remain readability heuristics.

Heading crossed by a wire; see also the [text/text case](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/51b1538f2bdf094a293e122c54939fad31b12596/tests/cases/__snapshots__/text-text-collision.snap.svg):

title: Add feedback-network and pull-resistor placement analyzers
description: Adds feedback-network and pull-resistor placement diagnostics to the default pipeline and fixes the existing capacitor-orientation check.
body:
Adds feedback-network and pull-resistor placement diagnostics to the default pipeline. Also fixes the existing capacitor-orientation check so a horizontal capacitor directly connecting an op-amp output to either input is accepted. The existing scattered-feedback repro now recommends grouping R1 closer to the amplifier; compact feedback capacitors keep their horizontal orientation without warnings. ## Behavior - **FeedbackNetworkPlacementSolver** emits `FeedbackNetworkNotCompact` for distant resistors/capacitors directly bridging a declared `simple_op_amp` output and inverting input. Parallel R/C feedback produces one issue naming the distant members. The bounding-box gap must exceed both 4 schematic units and three times the member’s largest dimension. - **PullResistorPlacementSolver** emits `PullResistorOnWrongSide` when an explicitly requested pull-up/down connects to the appropriate declared power/ground rail and its entire body lies more than 1.5 schematic units on the opposite side of the signal pin. Both produce advisory readability suggestions with structured component context and string output. They preserve the input circuit and respect sheet, subcircuit, and explicit group boundaries. Suggestions do not claim an unverified replacement position. ## Six layout cases Three snapshots per analyzer: one flagged layout and two readable controls. Each image stacks the generated schematic above its analysis. All four controls assert that the complete analysis is empty. The existing `feedback-network-scattered` snapshot and test are retained with their original resistor-only layout and updated analyzer output. No snapshots already present on main are deleted. Only the redundant cases added by this PR have been removed; compact R/C controls cover the capacitor-orientation fix. | Analyzer | Flagged layout | Readable control | Readable control | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Feedback | Existing scattered feedback
![Scattered feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/feedback-network-scattered.snap.svg) | Compact negative feedback
![Compact feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/feedback-network-compact.snap.svg) | Compact positive feedback
![Compact positive feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/feedback-network-positive-feedback.snap.svg) | | Pull resistors | Pulls on opposite sides
![Wrong-side pulls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pull-resistors-wrong-side.snap.svg) | Conventional vertical pulls
![Conventional pulls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pull-resistor-readable-layouts-conventional.snap.svg) | Horizontal pulls at signal level
![Horizontal pulls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/de4512267a3e6bcec4e12527301aba4f043f21e9/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pull-resistor-readable-layouts-horizontal.snap.svg) | ## Scope Feedback placement currently recognizes direct negative feedback on native op-amps. Generic chips, series feedback networks, and shared summing nodes are excluded. The positive-feedback control is now compact and readable; it also verifies that the capacitor-orientation exception accepts feedback to the non-inverting input. Positive-feedback distance analysis remains outside this initial scope. Pull recognition requires `needs_external_pullup`/`needs_external_pulldown`. Shared buses, conflicting or missing metadata, zero-ohm links, and other resistor/device branches are skipped. A local shunt capacitor to ground is allowed. The orientation exception does not include capacitors from the output to a declared ground/power rail. The saved real-project exports inspected lack the required op-amp/pull metadata, so positive coverage comes from the merged TSX repros and their variants. The thresholds are schematic readability heuristics. ## Validation - `bun test`: 50 passing entries; 11 unrelated existing `test.failing` cases remain. - `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass. - Stacked SVG snapshots and connectivity assertions for the six layouts; visually inspected the feedback layouts. All three feedback tests pass after restoring the original main-branch repro. - Existing standalone horizontal-capacitor and vertical-capacitor tests still pass.
